So integral or p-integral certificates exist iff this layered design system has such a solution; weak- and functional-PHP matching designs coincide. | Working proof (restatement; strengthened by the restriction argument), after a fresh-context review. | [Integral degree-two entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-integral-degree-two) |
| `prop:integral-degree-two-certificate` | Weak unary PHP^{n+1}_n, n >= 3, has an integer-valued degree-2 NS dual functional: l(x_ij) = [j = 0], and for pigeons i < i', l(x_i0 x_i'2) = l(x_i1 x_i'0) = 1, l(x_i1 x_i'2) = -1, else 0 (a spanning-tree solution of the zero-diagonal flow problem, totally unimodular at degree 2). For n = 2 the unique matching design is half-integral (3-integral, not 2-integral); d <= 1 is trivial. Hence conj:three-integral-php-certificates holds at every d <= 2. F_p hardness at degree 2 already follows from Razborov's bound; only integrality is new. | Working proof of an easy observation; checked over Z for n = 3..7; after a fresh-context review. | [Integral degree-two entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-integral-degree-two) |
| `thm:integral-design-extension` | Integral design extension: on a board with any number of pigeon rows and N hole columns, with A = Z or Z_(p), every degree-2 PHP matching design with values in A extends to a degree-R design with values in A when R >= 2 and N >= 2R - 1 (the F_2 boundary filling of prop:matching-moment-homology-extension with orientation signs (-1)^{row position}, and integral chessboard homology vanishing from the BLVZ connectivity theorem). Consequently weak unary PHP^{n+1}_n, n >= 3, has an integer-valued NS dual functional of degree floor((n+1)/2), and conj:three-integral-php-certificates holds for every d <= floor((n+1)/2), which for integer d equals Razborov's range d < n/2 + 1; above it the conjecture is open (the filling fails at k = R+1, where N >= 2k-1 fails). | Working proof, after a fresh-context review. | [Integral extension entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-integral-extension) |
| `conj:integral-certificates-dense-quadric` | For weak unary PHP^{n+1}_n plus one constraint q_L = (L - 1)(L - 2), L = c0 + sum_e a_e x_e with integer coefficients in {0,1,2} (a lift of L^2 - 1 mod 3), at every degree d <= floor((n+1)/2) where F_3 does not NS-refute, the constant monomial lies outside Sat(L_d) + 3 Z_(3)^N, i.e. a 3-integral rational NS certificate exists. Lift-dependent. | Conjecture; evidence: two seeds at 6 pigeons, degree 3 (ex:dense-quadric-integral-small), conditional on the rational rank. | [Dense-block integral entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-dense-block-integral) |
| `ex:dense-quadric-integral-small` | Weak PHP^6_5 plus one random dense constraint (L - 1)(L - 2) (20 of 30 variables, c0 = 0 and 1): NS degree 3 lattice has F_3 rank 3894 vs rational-rank estimate 3901 (eight modular ranks agree), 7 dimensions of 3-torsion; F_3, F_5, F_7 do not refute; one lifting step reaches 3901 and e_1 is outside the 3-saturation, so a 3-integral certificate exists (conditional on the rational rank). Seeds 2-5 not run (time limit). Control: 5 pigeons, F_3 refutes. | Finite check (two seeds; conditional on the rational rank). | [Dense-block integral entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-dense-block-integral) |
| `conj:integral-designs-aux-encoding` | For weak unary PHP^{n+1}_n plus one equation E = L - 1 - y - 3 sum_{i<r} 2^i b_i over fresh Boolean y, b_i (exact encoding of L != 0 mod 3; L = c0 + sum a_e x_e with integer coefficients in {0,1,2}, r large enough), at every NS degree d <= floor((n+1)/2) where F_3 does not refute, the constant monomial is outside Sat(L_d) + 3 Z_(3)^N, i.e. a 3-integral rational design exists. Proof route: the auxiliary-bit lifting is a weighted Koszul complex on r vertices. | Conjecture; evidence: 7 seeds at 6 pigeons, degree 3 (ex:aux-encoding-integral-small), conditional on the rational rank. | [Aux encoding entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-aux-encoding) |
| `ex:aux-encoding-integral-small` | Weak PHP^6_5 plus one random dense block (support 18-24 of 30 cells) encoded by L - 1 - y - 3 sum_{i<4} 2^i b_i = 0: at NS degree 3 (36 variables, 7176 monomials, 7117 multiples) all 7 seeds give F_3 rank 5514 and rational-rank estimate 5521 (F_5, F_7, 10^9+7), 7 dimensions of 3-torsion, no refutation over F_3, F_5, F_7, and e_1 outside the 3-saturation after one lifting step: a 3-integral design exists (conditional on the rational rank). Control: 5 pigeons, F_3 refutes. | Finite check (7 seeds; conditional on the rational rank). | [Aux encoding entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-aux-encoding) |
| `lem:auxiliary-bit-relaxation` | Auxiliary-bit relaxation (formal degrees): for weak unary PHP plus E = L - 1 - y - 3 sum_i 2^i b_i over fresh Booleans y, b_i, degree-d designs (over any commutative ring) vanishing on every monomial containing a bit correspond exactly to designs of PHP plus the multiples m (L-1)(L-2), deg m <= d-2, via l(my) = l(m(L-1)); a Z_(3)-valued design reduces mod 3, on bit-free monomials, to an F_3 design of PHP plus L = 1 + y (equivalently L^2 - 1), and blockwise for many encoded blocks. So integrality of such designs gives nothing for A1 without a characteristic-0 many-block mechanism. | Working proof, after a fresh-context review. | [Koszul lift entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-koszul-lift) |
| `prop:dense-blocks-outside-mn-framework` | In Miksa-Nordstrom's generalized Alekhnovich-Razborov framework (arXiv:1505.01358, Definitions 3.1-3.7, Theorem 3.8), a cluster B unforced by every single variable set (no assignment to one V satisfies B) is a disrespectful neighbour of every V it meets; families of unforced clusters have empty respectful boundary, and \|boundary(U')\| <= #{V disjoint from Vars(B)} for U' containing B; if B also meets every V, every U' containing B has empty boundary, so with at least s clusters xi >= delta s and Theorem 3.8's bound is negative. Application to W's dense-block clauses is conditional on joint feasibility (L_i = 0 with all prefix L_j != 0 after fixing any one small set) and on covering; the obstruction is relative to the choice of variable sets. | Working proof of the framework statement, after a fresh-context review; application to W conditional. | [MN operator entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-mn-operator) |
| `lem:reslin-weakening-admissible` | Weakening is admissible in Res(Lin_F_p): from a derivation of a line C using the linear-combination rule, removal of false constant equations and weakening, one obtains, line by line, a weakening-free derivation of some C' contained in C with at most as many lines (a rediscovery of the standard weakening elimination for resolution); refutations stay refutations. | Working proof of a standard lemma, after a fresh-context review. | [Derivation chooser entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-derivation-chooser) |
| `prop:inherited-prefixes-must-grow` | One-step inheritance obstruction: for a Res(Lin_F3) resolution step from blocks B1 (containing f, prefix S1) and B2 (containing g, prefix S2) to B3 = (B1 - f) u (B2 - g) u {alpha f + beta g} with prefix S3, where the premises share no forms apart from possibly f = g, if a non-prefix form w of B3 lies in S1 - f (or S2 - g) and some cube point has w = 0, every other premise form nonzero, and h nonzero if h is in S3, then w's W clause (w = 0 implies some S3 form = 0) is not implied on the cube by both premises' clauses, hence not derivable from them at any degree. So at such steps clause-inheriting choosers must keep the premises' surviving prefix forms. Fails without the no-sharing hypothesis (counterexample with g = w). | Working proof, after a fresh-context review. | [Derivation chooser entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-derivation-chooser) |
| `prop:symmetric-design-collapse` | Symmetric design collapse: over F_3, for any system on an m x N board containing Booleanity, collisions and linear rows sum_j x_ij = 1 (optionally onto columns and functionality), with s0 = N mod 3 in {0,1,2} and m > s0, no Nullstellensatz design of total degree s0+1 is invariant under S_m x S_N (the absent-pigeon row equation (N-s) l(lambda+{1}) = l(lambda) vanishes at s = s0 and forces l(1) = 0); designs averaged over a group of order prime to 3 remain designs, so a design exists iff a G-invariant one does for such G. | Working proof (elementary, likely folklore). | [Symmetric-designs entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-symmetric-designs) |
| `ex:onto-ns-degree-small-boards` | Finite check over F_3 in Sylow 2-orbit coordinates: onto weak PHP (Booleanity, collisions, rows and onto columns, no functionality) and weak PHP with m = N+3 are both first Nullstellensatz-refuted at total degree 3 on 6x3 and 7x4 and at degree 5 (not 4) on 9x6; on 10x7 the onto system has no refutation of total degree 5 (weak control at 10x7 not reached, degree 6 not reached); controls: onto with functionality falls at 3 and functionality alone at 4 on 8x5. | Exact GF(3) finite check (FLINT rref over Sylow 2-orbits; agrees with unsymmetrized runs and recorded PC closures on the small boards). | [Symmetric-designs entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-symmetric-designs) |
| `thm:spare-pigeon-onto-hardness` | Spare-pigeon theorem: over any field of characteristic p > 0, onto weak PHP O_{m,N} (Booleanity, collisions, linear rows sum_j x_ij = 1, linear onto columns sum_i x_ij = 1, no functionality) with m = N (mod p) and N >= 3 has no PC refutation of degree <= ceil(N/2). Proof: the substitution x_{m,j} -> 1 - sum_{i<m} y_ij (a fat spare pigeon taking every free hole) maps a degree-D refutation to one of weak PHP^{m-1}_N of degree max(D,2), which has fewer axioms than the functional PHP of Impagliazzo-Pudlak-Sgall (ECCC TR97-042, Theorem 2.9: no refutation of degree <= ceil(N/2) over any field). | Working proof (elementary reduction plus an imported theorem), after two fresh-context reviews. | [Spare-pigeon entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-spare-pigeon) |
| `cor:column-statistic-families-random-prefix` | Column-statistic families under random prefixes: conj:occupancy-pinned-php holds for n >= 5 with e = 2 and c = 1/3 (every PC refutation of the pinned system has degree >= ceil((n-2)/2)+1, by restriction to O_{n+1,n-2} and thm:spare-pigeon-onto-hardness); hence by prop:occupancy-pin-reduction, if 4t+2 <= ceil((n-2)/2) and 11 max(1,delta) <= ceil((n-2)/2), for each family of M <= n^K blocks fixed before the prefixes are drawn whose forms lie in the span of the column sums and rho further forms, W_RS holds with probability >= 1 - M 3^(rho-t), which is 1 - o(1) for t >= (K+1) log_3 n + omega(1) and rho = O(1) (or rho <= t - K log_3 n - omega(1)); this includes column statistics over any number of holes. | Working proof (composition of recorded results), after a fresh-context review. | [Spare-pigeon entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-spare-pigeon) |
| `lem:spare-pigeon-composition` | Spare-pigeon composition: over F_3, for any family F of blocks on the (n+1) x n board and any pigeon s, a degree-D PC refutation of the pinned system (conj:occupancy-pinned-php, e = 2) plus F's randomized-prefix clauses gives one of degree max(D,2) of weak PHP of the n pigeons other than s into the n-2 non-empty holes plus the clauses of sigma_s(F) with the same prefix matrices, where sigma_s sets the empty holes' cells to 0 and x_sj -> 1 - sum_{i != s} x_ij; supp sigma_s(b) <= \|U_b\| + n \|U_b cap row s\|. | Working proof (composition of thm:spare-pigeon-onto-hardness's substitution with restriction), after a fresh-context review. | [Composed-pins entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-composed-pins) |
| `prop:light-spare-composition` | Light-spare composition (conditional): over F_3, for a family L u S fixed in advance, L light (\|U_b\| <= n^{2-eta}) and S of rank <= rho modulo the column sums, if some pigeon s has \|U_b cap row s\| <= n^{1-eta} for all b in L, then W_RS holds at degree B = max(11 max(1,delta), 4t+2) with failure probability <= \|S\| 3^{rho-t} + o(1), provided thm:random-prefix-light-families holds for weak PHP^{N+2}_N (N = n-2). Families whose heavy rows cover every pigeon row defeat the choice of s; for them the mixed case is open. | Condition discharged by thm:random-prefix-light-families-imbalance; unconditional form thm:light-column-mixed-families. | [Composed-pins entry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-26-composed-pins) |
| `lem:cube-odd-generator-criterion` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, for e >= 2, with s the solution of P_e P_{e+1} and t that of P_{e-1} P_{e+2} at (2e+1, 2): (W_e) holds iff some quartic form alpha makes F_2 divide every coordinate of t - alpha s, where F_2 is the product of the three linear forms y1 +- y2 +- y3 through the double points; equivalently the ratio t/s on each of the three lines, where c is 2-torsion, is a binary quartic and the three agree at the double points. | Working proof from lem:cube-general-peeling, lem:cube-boundary-generators-coprime, lem:cube-excess-sum-basis and lem:cube-threshold-ideal; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Odd generator criterion](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-odd-generator-criterion) |
| `check:cube-odd-generator-seven-two` | Over F_1000003 the S_3-invariant witnesses of excess 24 at (7,2), m = 29, form a 2-dimensional space whose solutions have value rank 2 at a random point, so (W_3) holds modulo the computing prime with an invariant generator. | Finite check by the chunked sym val mode of bmd_cube_solution_cones (FLINT), validated on (3,2) and (5,2); no rational lift. | [Odd generator criterion](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-odd-generator-criterion) |
| `lem:cube-odd-generator-poles` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, for e >= 2 and each line l of F_2 = 0: the ratio lambda_l = t/s of the solutions of P_{e-1}P_{e+2} and P_e P_{e+1} at (2e+1,2) is regular on l except possibly at its four collision points (two double points and two further points) and at the finite sets Z_e, Z_{e+1} where boundary solutions vanish; on l outside Z_2 and the relevant Z_n, where c is 2-torsion, phi_{n+2} = mu_n psi phi_n for a fixed psi, and lambda_l = mu_e/mu_{e-1} (ratios of the mu_n are well defined). | Working proof by injectivity of residue duality and the divisors of the boundary functions when 2c = 0; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Odd generator poles](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-odd-generator-poles) |
| `lem:cube-collision-point-regularity` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2: a boundary witness P_n not containing a smooth conic through the four vertices of a coordinate plane or of the plane z1 = z2 meets it at the origin with order <= n^2 + 2n; at the non-double collision points (1:-1:0) and (1:1:2) of the line y3 = y1 + y2 the curve z(T) runs along such conics, so if W^(e) and W^(e+1) are nonzero there (equivalently P_e, P_{e+1} do not contain the conics), s = W^{P_e P_{e+1}} is nonzero and t/s is regular; P_n contains only finitely many conics of each pencil. | Working proof by Bezout on the conics and the collision-free lemma; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Collision points](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-points) |
| `check:cube-boundary-collision-values` | Over F_1000003, for n = 2..5 the boundary solution W^(n) (found in the S_3-trivial part) is nonzero at (1,-1,0) and (1,1,2) and zero at the double point (0,1,1); by the boundary theorem this transfers to characteristic 0 and almost every p. | Finite check by the fixed-point value mode of bmd_cube_solution_cones in series mode. | [Collision points](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-points) |
| `lem:cube-line-gcd-criterion` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, for e >= 2: if P_p lies in J^{psi(p)} (psi(p) = floor(p^2/2)) for p = e-1..e+2 and, for n = e, e+1, the gcd of the coordinates of the boundary solution W^(n) along the line y = (u, 1, u+1) of F_2 = 0 is u^{psi(n)} (and the same at u = infinity), then (W_e) holds: t/s is a quartic on each line of F_2 = 0 vanishing at the double points. | Working proof from lem:cube-odd-generator-criterion, lem:cube-odd-generator-poles, lem:cube-collision-point-regularity and lem:cube-product-cone-formula, with the order comparison psi(e-1)+psi(e+2) = psi(e)+psi(e+1)+2; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Double points](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-double-points) |
| `thm:cube-odd-generators-small` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic 0 and in characteristic p outside a finite set, (W_3) and (W_4) hold; hence every pair with 2 <= rho <= d-1 and d <= 5 rho has a free solution module with least excess B, and l_0(d+1, 4d+rho-1) = B(d, rho) for all rho >= d/5. | Working proof by lem:cube-line-gcd-criterion with its conditions checked for n <= 5 modulo 1000003 (check:cube-boundary-line-gcd) and the vertex-line theorem for P_6, transferred to characteristic 0 and almost every p, then thm:cube-peeling-reduction part 2; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Double points](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-double-points) |
| `check:cube-boundary-line-gcd` | Over F_1000003, for n = 2..5: the witness space at (n,1), excess n^2-1, is one-dimensional and S_3-trivial, its jet lies in J^{psi(n)}, its cone of order psi(n) at (1:1:0) is nonzero in the direction of a line of F_2 = 0, and the gcd of the coordinates of W^(n) along y = (u,1,u+1) is u^{psi(n)} (u^2, u^4, u^8, u^12). | Finite check by bmd_cube_solution_cones (series mode, fixed cone direction, value dumps) and bmd_cube_line_gcd.py. | [Double points](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-double-points) |
| `lem:cube-residue-disc-valuation` | On {0,1}^3: let O be a complete DVR with residue characteristic != 2, K = Frac O, y in O^3, and P a polynomial with coefficients in O and h_P = T^{-k} P(z) / prod L'(z_i) nonzero, expanded at p_0 on the branch z_i = r_0(y_i T). If no zero of phi_P = T^{-k} P(z) on the curve w_i^2 = 1 + 4 y_i T over the algebraic closure lies in the residue disc of p_0 (\|T\| < 1, all w_i = 1 mod the maximal ideal), then the lowest nonzero Laurent coefficient of h_P has the least valuation among all its coefficients. | Working proof by Weierstrass preparation in O[[T]]: a smaller valuation beyond the leading term gives a distinguished factor whose root is a zero of phi_P in the disc; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Residue disc](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-residue-disc) |
| `lem:cube-line-gcd-sufficiency` | On {0,1}^3, for e >= 2, in characteristic 0 or odd p with p not dividing n or p = n for n = e-1..e+2: if for n = e, e+1 the gcd of the coordinates of the boundary solution W^(n) along y = (u, 1, u+1) is u^{psi(n)}, psi(n) = floor(n^2/2), then (W_e) holds. The vertex-line hypothesis P_p in J^{psi(p)} of lem:cube-line-gcd-criterion is not needed. | Working proof: lem:cube-residue-disc-valuation on F[[u]] at the double points of the line, with the zeros of phi_n on the lines of F_2 = 0 at T = infinity or at 2-torsion points sigma_i sigma_j(p_0), and the boundary coordinate theorem; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Residue disc](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-residue-disc) |
| `thm:cube-odd-generators-seven` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic 0 and in characteristic p != 3 outside a finite set, (W_e) holds for e <= 7; hence l_0(d+1, 4d+rho-1) = B(d, rho) for every pair with 2 <= rho <= d-1 and d <= 8 rho. | Working proof by lem:cube-line-gcd-sufficiency, with the line-gcd property for n <= 5 from thm:cube-odd-generators-small and for n = 6, 7, 8 from the maximal-minor gcds of the route review modulo 1000003, made exact by lem:cube-gcd-all-m and the boundary coordinate theorem and transferred by the primitive gcd form; then thm:cube-peeling-reduction part 2 with e = 7; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Residue disc](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-residue-disc) |
| `thm:cube-line-gcd-all` | On {0,1}^3, for every n >= 1, in characteristic 0 or odd p with p not dividing n or p = n: along the line y_3 = y_1 + y_2 of F_2 = 0 the coordinate W_{c_n} (c_n = 4n for odd n, 4n-1 for even n) of the primitive boundary solution W^(n) restricts to a nonzero constant times (y_1 y_2)^{psi(n)}, psi(n) = floor(n^2/2), and the gcd over F[u] of the coordinates of W^(n)(u, 1, u+1) is u^{psi(n)}; likewise on the other two lines. | Working proof by a degree count: deg W_{c_n} = 2 psi(n), order >= psi(n) at both double points of the line (boundary coordinate theorem), and W_{c_n} nonzero on the line because phi_n has pole order exactly 4n+1 or 4n there; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Line-gcd proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-line-gcd-proof) |
| `thm:cube-torsion-partition-char-zero` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic 0, for all 1 <= rho <= d the solution module at m = 4d+rho-1 is free and l_0(d+1, 4d+rho-1) = B(d, rho), the sum of pi_i^2 - 1 over the balanced partition of d into rho parts; in odd characteristic p outside the finite set of thm:cube-peeling-reduction, l_0 = B(d, rho) for 2 <= rho <= d-1 with d <= (2p-2) rho (freeness not claimed there). | Working proof: thm:cube-line-gcd-all and lem:cube-line-gcd-sufficiency give (W_e) for every e >= 2 in characteristic 0 (for e <= 2p-3 in characteristic p), then thm:cube-peeling-reduction parts 2 and 3; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Line-gcd proof](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-line-gcd-proof) |
| `thm:cube-dimension-three-per-order` | On {0,1}^3 over a field of characteristic 0, for k >= 1, 0 <= l <= k-1 and m = k-l-1: delta(3,k,l) = 2k+1-h with h = 0 if m = 0 and otherwise h = 1 + max{d in [0, floor(m/4)] : 5d <= m+1, or 5d > m+1 and B(d, m+1-4d) <= l}, B(d,rho) = sum(pi_i^2 - 1) over the balanced partition of d into rho parts; the same holds in odd characteristic p outside the finite set of thm:cube-peeling-reduction whenever m <= 16p-12. | Working proof assembling lem:cube-threshold-ideal, thm:finite-grid-stable-law, thm:cube-dimension-three-law (kappa_3), thm:cube-order-zero-value and thm:cube-torsion-partition-char-zero; matches all 462 recorded exact kernel values over F_3, F_5, F_7 and F_101; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Dimension-3 formula](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-formula) |
| `lem:cube-double-point-order-reduction` | On {0,1}^3 over every field of characteristic != 2 and for every n >= 1, every coordinate of the primitive boundary solution W^(n) vanishes to order >= floor(n^2/2) at each double point (1:1:0), (1:0:1), (0:1:1). | Working proof: characteristic 0 is thm:cube-boundary-coordinate-order part 3; in characteristic p the reduction of the primitive integral solution is a nonzero constant times the primitive solution mod p (rank-1 kernel, equal degrees), and vanishing Taylor coefficients at an integral point reduce; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Odd characteristic](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-odd-characteristic) |
| `thm:cube-torsion-partition-odd` | On {0,1}^3: (W_e) holds for every e >= 2 in every odd characteristic; and in odd characteristic p outside the finite exceptional set E of thm:cube-diagonal-near-diagonal, every solution module at 1 <= rho <= d is free, l_0(d+1, 4d+rho-1) = B(d, rho), and the formula of thm:cube-dimension-three-per-order gives delta_F(3,k,l) for all k, l. | Working proof: lem:cube-double-point-order-reduction makes thm:cube-line-gcd-all and lem:cube-line-gcd-sufficiency characteristic-free; thm:cube-peeling-reduction uses the (5,2) theorem only for (W_2), so its exceptional set reduces to that of thm:cube-half-plane, which is E; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Odd characteristic](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-odd-characteristic) |
| `thm:cube-diagonal-every-odd` | On {0,1}^3 over every field of characteristic != 2 the solution modules at (2,2), (3,2), (3,3) are free on generators of excesses {0,2}, {3,4}, {0,2,3}; hence the hypotheses (i)-(iii) of thm:cube-diagonal-near-diagonal hold and that theorem has no exceptional characteristic. | Working proof with an exact certificate (Macaulay2): over QQ, minimal generators whose primitive integral lifts have minor contents 150, 25, 168750 (odd primes 3, 5 only), so their reductions are bases for every other odd p by the basis criterion; over ZZ/3 and ZZ/5 the minimal generators are computed directly; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Diagonal certificate](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-diagonal-certificate) |
| `thm:cube-dimension-three-every-field` | On {0,1}^3 over every field of characteristic != 2: every solution module at 1 <= rho <= d is free with l_0(d+1, 4d+rho-1) = B(d, rho), and delta_F(3,k,l) = 2k+1-h with h = 0 if m = k-l-1 = 0 and otherwise h-1 the larger of floor((m+1)/5) and the largest d <= floor(m/4) with 5d > m+1 and B(d, m+1-4d) <= l. | Working proof: thm:cube-dimension-three-per-order in characteristic 0; thm:cube-torsion-partition-odd in odd characteristic, whose exceptional set is emptied by thm:cube-diagonal-every-odd; agrees with all 918 recorded exact kernel values; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Diagonal certificate](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-diagonal-certificate) |
| `lem:cube-line-threshold-bound` | On {0,1}^n over any field: if some element of I^{(h)}_m of degree l_0(h,m) does not vanish on the line y = au+bv (as for a generic line), the ideal of top coordinates of the kernel of A_m restricted to that line has initial degree <= l_0(h,m). | Working proof: substitution commutes with the linear system and keeps homogeneity and excess. | [Dimension four](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-dimension-four) |
| `check:cube-dimension-four-thresholds` | On {0,1}^4 over F_32003: l_0(3,13) = 12 (no solution of excess <= 8 at m = 13; syzygies up to excess 15 of excesses 12, 13, 14, 14, 15), line values 4, 2, 1 at m = 14, 15, 16 (lower bounds for lines outside a proper closed set); on a random line the m = 13 kernel splits as (7,7), so the global module there is not free if the line is generic; dimension-3 controls reproduce B(d,rho) globally for d = 3 and on the line for d <= 4. | Finite check by Macaulay2 graded kernels (research/tools/bmd_cube_thresholds_m2.m2), global, degree-limited and on a random line. | [Dimension four](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-dimension-four) |
| `check:cube-dimension-four-generators` | On {0,1}^4 over F_32003, the savings-3 threshold generators are: at m = 17 and 18 (l_0 = 2) scalar multiples of the S_4-invariant irreducible quadric Q = sum_{i<j} y_i y_j - 2 sum_i y_i^2; at m = 16 (l_0 = 5) three irreducible quintics; at m = 15 (l_0 = 6) one irreducible sextic. | Finite check by Macaulay2 (incremental degree-limited syzygies, factorization of top coordinates). | [Dimension-four quadric](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-dimension-four-quadric) |

| `lem:cube-symmetric-reduction` | On {0,1}^n over a field, S_n acts on the solutions of the threshold system by (sigma W)_c(y) = W_c(sigma^{-1} y), preserving excess, so I^{(h)}_m is S_n-stable; if n! is invertible, the S_n-invariant elements of I^{(h)}_m of degree l are exactly the top coordinates of the S_n-invariant solutions of excess l. | Working proof by the row-permutation identity and the Reynolds operator; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Symmetric kernel](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-symmetric-kernel) |

Controls: the 2-torsion cubic L_2 at (3,13) in dimension 3, and Q at m = 17, 18 and the threshold 6 at m = 15 in dimension 4. | Finite check by the FLINT symmetric kernel research/tools/bmd_cube_symmetric_solutions.cpp, validated on the controls. | [Symmetric kernel](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-symmetric-kernel) |
| `thm:cube-branch-point-symmetry` | On {0,1}^n over every field of characteristic != 2, every threshold ideal I^{(d+1)}_m is stable under the linear involution psi(y) = (y_1, y_1-y_2, ..., y_1-y_n), with W_m -> +-W_m o psi on homogeneous solutions of the same excess; since the ideals are homogeneous and psi = -s_{01}, they are stable under S_{n+1} permuting the branch points 0, y_1, ..., y_n (the reflection representation); <S_n, psi> = S_{n+1} x {+-1} for n >= 2. | Working proof: the Moebius substitution T -> -T/(1+4y_1T) fixes p_0, maps V_d(y) onto w_1^{-d} V_d(psi(y)) since div w_1 = H_1 - H_inf, and acts on solution windows by unimodular triangular matrices preserving the top coordinate up to sign; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Branch-point symmetry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-branch-point-symmetry) |
| `cor:cube-quadric-threshold-d3` | On {0,1}^4 over F_32003: l_0(4,38) = 2 and l_0(3,17) = l_0(3,18) = 2; the degree-2 part of the threshold ideal there is the line of Q = sum_{i<j} y_i y_j - 2 sum y_i^2 plus possibly a [3,2] component of S_5. | Working proof from thm:cube-branch-point-symmetry and the S_4-invariant computations of check:cube-quadric-d3 (I_1 is 0 or all of the irreducible reflection representation, and has no S_4-invariant element). | [Branch-point symmetry](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-branch-point-symmetry) |
| `lem:cube-generic-normality` | For every n >= 1 and every degree vector (nu_r)_{r in {0,1}^n} with nu_r >= -1, the determinant Delta_nu(a) of the coefficients of T^0..T^{N-1} in T^j w^r (j <= nu_r, w_i = (1+a_iT)^{1/2}, N = sum(nu_r+1)) is a nonzero polynomial over Z[1/2]: in characteristic 0 every multi-index is normal for the system {w^r} at generic centres, and for fixed nu the same holds in odd characteristic outside a finite set of primes. | Working proof: the Wronskian of T^j w^r on the curve w_i^2 = 1+a_iT is nonzero in characteristic 0, and the transport to a general point q gives Delta_nu(a/(1+aT(q))) != 0. | [Exact collision exponents](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-exponents-exact) |
| `thm:cube-boundary-collision-exponents` | On {0,1}^n in characteristic 0, n >= 2, d >= 1, N = N_{2,n}(d) and every m >= N-1: along each collision divisor y_i = 0 or y_i = y_j the nonzero elementary divisors of the N x (m+1) constraint matrix are exactly the d - e(P), so the gcd g_{n,d} of the boundary minors and Delta_{n,d} both have exponent E_n(d) = sum_k C(n-1,k) floor((d-k+1)^2/4) there; hence l_0(d+1,N) = deg Delta_{n,d} - C(n+1,2) E_n(d) - deg g^nc, which on {0,1}^4 (d >= 2) is 10d^2 - 10d - 5 - deg g^nc_{4,d}, with g^nc the part of g prime to the collision forms. For fixed (n,d) the exponents hold in odd characteristic outside finitely many primes. | Working proof: the collision limit lemma's basis of the saturation, normality of its limit space from lem:cube-generic-normality, saturation at every truncation m >= N-1, and the Moebius transport; the closed forms are asserted by research/tools/bmd_cube_collision_counts.py. | [Exact collision exponents](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-exponents-exact) |
| `prop:cube-extra-factors-double` | On {0,1}^n in characteristic 0 (n >= 2, d >= 1), every prime factor of the boundary gcd g_{n,d} other than the collision forms divides Delta_{n,d} at least twice; hence if the non-collision part of Delta_{n,d} is squarefree, l_0(d+1, N_{2,n}(d)) = deg Delta_{n,d} - C(n+1,2) E_n(d), which is 10d^2 - 10d - 5 on {0,1}^4 for d >= 2. | Working proof: at a general point of such a factor, p_0 has top order >= N+1 and so weight >= 2; the Wronskian's order at p_0 equals the order in t of Delta along the transport curve a/(1+at), which is transversal to the factor because it is not invariant under the flow of sum a_i^2 d/da_i. | [Exact collision exponents](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-exponents-exact) |

Its dimension-four characteristic-zero part is now extended to every d>=2 by cor:cube-four-boundary-law; the older dimension-five and positive-characteristic scope is unchanged. | [Dimension-4 boundary](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-dimension-four-boundary) |

| `lem:cube-quadrangle-diagonal` | Over a field of characteristic 0 (or p not dividing 2 mu), no form of degree mu >= 1 on P^2 restricts on each of the six sides of a complete quadrangle to a nonzero multiple of the mu-th power of the linear form vanishing at that side's diagonal point: if each restriction is kappa_ij times that power, all kappa_ij = 0. | Working proof by coordinates A_i = coordinate points and (1:1:1), and a two-coefficient comparison on the side x = z; checked for mu <= 7 by exact linear algebra. | [Squarefree reduction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-squarefree-reduction) |
| `lem:cube-no-double-double-surface` | For n >= 3 in characteristic 0, no homogeneous polynomial of positive degree in y_1..y_n restricts on every collision hyperplane D_ab = {r_a = r_b} to a nonzero constant times a product of double-double forms r_z - r_w ({z,w} disjoint from {a,b}). | Working proof: the lowest part of the local expansion at a general point of a quadruple stratum through a double-double factor (so the order is >= 1), restricted to a transverse 3-space, contradicts lem:cube-quadrangle-diagonal. | [Squarefree reduction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-squarefree-reduction) |
| `thm:cube-squarefree-reduction` | In characteristic 0, n >= 4, d >= 1: Delta_U = c prod_{j>=2} y_j^{2E_n(d)} prod_{2<=i<j} (y_i-y_j)^{E_n(d)} Delta^nc_{n,d}\|_{y_1=0} for the collision limit space U^{(n-1)}_d; and if Delta_U has multiplicity exactly 2E_n(d) along each y_j and a squarefree part prime to the collision forms of y_2..y_n, then Delta^nc_{n,d} is squarefree, g_{n,d} = c' prod l_D^{E_n(d)} and l_0(d+1, N) = deg Delta_{n,d} - C(n+1,2) E_n(d) (10d^2 - 10d - 5 for n = 4). | Working proof from the collision lifts and limit lemmas, thm:cube-boundary-collision-exponents, the S_{n+1} transport, lem:cube-no-double-double-surface and prop:cube-extra-factors-double. | [Squarefree reduction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-squarefree-reduction) |

| `lem:cube-confluence-valuation` | In characteristic 0, for every n >= 1 and degree vector nu on {0,1}^n (alpha_{r'} = nu_{(r',0)}, beta_{r'} = nu_{(r',1)}), a_n^{e(nu)} with e(nu) = sum_{r'} (alpha_{r'}+1)(beta_{r'}+1) exactly divides the Hermite-Pade determinant Delta_nu of {T^j w^r}, and (Delta_nu / a_n^{e(nu)}) at a_n = 0 is a nonzero rational multiple of Delta_{nu'}(a_1..a_{n-1}) with nu'_{r'} = alpha_{r'} + beta_{r'} + 1; the one-variable systems {A + B(1+U)^{1/2}} are normal for all degree pairs. | Working proof: one-variable normality by a first-order differential elimination, then a row change to the order-adapted basis f_k(a_n T) of each block and the binomial identity C(a+b+2,2) - C(a+1,2) - C(b+1,2) = (a+1)(b+1). | [Confluence](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-confluence) |

| `check:cube-degree-vector-squarefree` | On one line over F_1000003, the non-collision part of the Hermite-Pade determinant Delta_nu is squarefree for all 194 monotone and 1093 of 1097 non-monotone degree vectors nu in {-1..4}^4 (n = 2, N >= 2) and for 52 vectors with n = 3 (the cube's vectors for d <= 6 and 40 random ones); the exceptions (3,0,1,1), (3,3,4,1) and their swaps have the factor (3a_1 + a_2)^3 exactly over Q, refuting squarefreeness for all degree vectors. | Finite check by the FLINT kernel research/tools/bmd_cube_nu_squarefree.cpp, validated against the z-basis limit data of route review 15, with exact sympy factorizations for n = 2; evidence rather than certificates where collision multiplicities over Q are unknown. | [Monotone squarefree](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-monotone-squarefree) |
| `conj:cube-monotone-squarefree` | In characteristic 0, for every n >= 1 and every monotone degree vector nu (nu_r >= nu_r' for r <= r', entries >= -1, N >= 1), the part of the Hermite-Pade determinant Delta_nu of {T^j w^r : j <= nu_r}, w_i = (1+a_iT)^{1/2}, prime to the collision forms a_i and a_i - a_j is squarefree; it contains conj:cube-boundary-squarefree and the open half of conj:cube-limit-determinant-squarefree. | Conjecture; the case n = 2, nu_r = d - \|r\| is proved for every d by thm:cube-conic-squarefree (entry-2026-09-26-cube-conic-squarefree); otherwise check:cube-degree-vector-squarefree (all 207 monotone vectors tested pass; non-monotone vectors can fail). | [Monotone squarefree](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-monotone-squarefree) |

| `lem:cube-residue-duality-all-n` | For n >= 3, d > n-3, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic != 2 at y with distinct nonzero entries where A_m(y) has rank N (m >= N-1): the residues Res_{p_0}(T^c eta), c <= m, identify the differentials with div eta >= d H_inf - (m+1) p_0 on the fibre curve (genus 1 + 2^{n-2}(n-3), K ~ (n-3) H_inf) with ker A_m(y); the solutions are Laurent tails of phi omega_0, phi in L((n-3-d) H_inf + (m+1) p_0); W_0 = 0 and W_m != 0 iff phi has pole order m+1. | Working proof as for lem:cube-residue-duality, with V_d = L(d H_inf) from N_{2,n}(d) = 2^{n-1} d + 1 - g and Riemann-Roch, and K ~ (n-3) H_inf from the complete intersection of n-1 quadrics. | [Middle-range height](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-middle-range-height) |

Radicality, the reduced-closure identification and uniform first initial degrees for d>=3 remain open. | [First-step curve](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-first-step-curve) |
| `lem:cube-first-step-sandwich` | Over any field, for all n, d >= 1 and every point y*, the zero set of the first-step threshold ideal I = I^{(d+1)}_{N+1} satisfies {rank A_N < N, rank A_{N+1} = N} subset V(I) subset {rank A_N < N}. | Working proof: I = (Im A_N : a), which is the unit ideal locally where A_N has full rank; and where rank A_N < N but rank A_{N+1} = N the two-dimensional kernel of A_{N+1}(y*) consists of padded kernel vectors of A_N(y*), whose last coordinate is 0. | [First-step sandwich](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-first-step-sandwich) |
| `cor:cube-first-step-brill-noether` | For n >= 3, d > n-3, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic != 2, at y* with distinct nonzero entries: rank A_m(y*) = N - h^0(d H_inf - (m+1) p_0) on the fibre curve, so y* is outside V(I^{(d+1)}_{N+1}) when h^0(d H_inf - (N+1) p_0) = 0 and inside it when that is >= 1 while h^0(d H_inf - (N+2) p_0) = 0 (classes of degree g-2 and g-3). | Working proof from lem:cube-first-step-sandwich and V_d = L(d H_inf) of lem:cube-residue-duality-all-n. | [First-step sandwich](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-first-step-sandwich) |
| `lem:cube-threshold-sandwich` | Over any field, for all n, d >= 1, m > N_{2,n}(d) and every point y*: {rank A_{m-1} < N, rank A_m = N} subset V(I^{(d+1)}_m) subset {rank A_{m-1} < N}. | Working proof: I_m = (Im A_{m-1} : a); local surjectivity where A_{m-1} has full rank; and a kernel-dimension count where A_{m-1} drops rank but A_m does not. | [Threshold support](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-threshold-support) |
| `thm:cube-threshold-collision-support` | For n >= 3, d > n-3, m > N in characteristic != 2: at y with distinct nonzero entries, y is outside V(I^{(d+1)}_m) if h^0(d H_inf - m p_0) = 0 and inside if that is >= 1 while h^0(d H_inf - (m+1) p_0) = 0; the class has degree 2^{n-1} d - m = g-1-(m-N), so for m > 2^{n-1} d every threshold ideal vanishes only on collision hyperplanes (a Brill-Noether regime of g-1 steps, then a collision regime; all collision regime for n = 3). | Working proof from lem:cube-threshold-sandwich and V_d = L(d H_inf) with rank A_k(y) = N - h^0(d H_inf - (k+1) p_0). | [Threshold support](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-threshold-support) |
| `thm:cube-collision-regime-torsion` | On {0,1}^4 in characteristic != 2 with d >= 2: at a point (0, y') of a collision hyperplane with y' distinct nonzero, the threshold ideal I^{(d+1)}_m is the unit ideal unless the collision limit space U_d(y') has an element of order >= m; since U_d(y') lies in L(2d H_inf) on the genus-1 limit curve, this never happens for m >= 8d+1, and at m = 8d only where 2d [H_inf - 4 p_0] = 0; so for m >= 8d+1 the zero sets of the threshold ideals lie in the 25 lines where collision hyperplanes meet. | Working proof: the polynomial factorization A = S Delta_1 A^Lambda from the collision lifts, the limit rows at y_1 = 0, the degree bound on the genus-1 curve, S_5 symmetry and thm:cube-threshold-collision-support. | [Collision regime](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-regime) |
| `lem:cube-point-window-membership` | On {0,1}^n over a field of characteristic != 2, for d >= 1, m >= 0, a point P and an arc through P with nonzero pairwise distinct coordinates: for every g in V (x) F((eps)) whose truncation tau_m(g) is integral, every solution W of the (d+1)-system at m has W(P) killing the reduction of tau_m(g); so if the span of these reductions over some arcs contains T^m (in particular if the span of the arc-limit spaces at P has an element of T-order exactly m), then P lies in V(I^{(d+1)}_m). | Working proof: substitute the arc into the identities A_m W = 0, extend F((eps))-linearly, reduce modulo eps, and use the threshold-ideal lemma. | [Collision windows](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-windows) |
| `check:cube-collision-regime-empty-d2` | On {0,1}^4 over F_32003 at d = 2: the kernel generators of excess <= 4 at m = 17 (6) and m = 18 (13) have top coordinates of degrees 2, 3, 4 generating a saturated ideal J whose zero set is 24 points on no collision hyperplane, the S_5-orbit of the pentagon configuration r_i = zeta^i; with the collision-support theorem, V(I^{(3)}_17) = V(I^{(3)}_18) = empty. | Finite check by research/tools/bmd_cube_collision_zero_sets.m2 (Macaulay2); J is contained in I_m, and thm:cube-threshold-collision-support puts V(I_m) in the collision hyperplanes for m > 16. | [Collision windows](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-windows) |

| `conj:cube-collision-regime-windows` | On {0,1}^4 in characteristic 0, for d >= 3 and m >= 8d+1, V(I^{(d+1)}_m) is the union of the 15 double-double lines if m <= 10d-8 and of the 10 triple-double points if m <= 10d-6, and is empty for m >= 10d-5; equivalently a point lies in V(I_m) exactly when the span of all arc limits there has an element of order m, the maximal orders being 10d-8 on double-double lines, 10d-6 at triple-double points, N at quadruple points and N-1 elsewhere on triple lines. | Partly refuted by ex:cube-collision-windows-slope (entry-2026-09-26-cube-triple-double-windows): the triple-double points lie in V(I_m) for m <= 11d - 12, so the triple-double value 10d - 6 and the emptiness claim fail for d >= 7; the double-double and triple-line parts remain conjectural, evidence d <= 5 in characteristic 1000003. | [Collision windows](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-collision-windows) |
| `lem:cube-isotypic-detection` | On {0,1}^n in characteristic 0 or p > n+1, for nu a partition of n, mu = nu with a part 1 added, and e >= 0: if every lambda of n+1 with n(lambda) = sum (i-1) lambda_i <= e dominates mu, then the degree-e part of I^{(h)}_m is nonzero iff some S_nu-invariant solution of excess e has nonzero top coordinate; so S_n-invariant solutions decide l_0 <= 1 for every n, and for n = 4 S_3-, S_2 x S_2- and S_2-invariant solutions decide every e <= 3, 5, 9. | Working proof: S_{n+1}-stability of I_m, Chevalley's decomposition with fake degrees (U_lambda first occurs in degree n(lambda)), Young's rule, and Reynolds averaging over S_nu. | [Invariant thresholds](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-invariant-thresholds) |

| `conj:cube-invariant-attainment` | On {0,1}^n in characteristic 0 or p > n+1, for every h >= 1 and m >= 0, the initial degree l_0(h,m) of the threshold ideal I^{(h)}_m is attained by an S_n-invariant element, so it equals the least excess of an S_n-invariant solution with nonzero top coordinate. | Proved in the full recorded scope and more: thm:cube-symmetric-flat-descent shows the entire kernel and marked top ideal arise by graded free extension from F[e1..en] in every odd characteristic, including primes dividing n!. | `lem:cube-boundary-generator-invariant` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, for every d >= 1 the generator D_d = Delta_{3,d}/g_{3,d} of the principal boundary threshold ideal I^{(d+1)}_{4d} is S_4-invariant and vanishes identically on no collision line. | Working proof: I_N principal (rank-1 reflexive), so D_d is a semi-invariant; a sign-type semi-invariant vanishes on every mirror; by the collision lifts, D_d is nonzero at a general point of y_3 = 0 because the genus-0 collision limit U_d misses the order-4d function psi^(2d), whose w_1 w_2 T^(d-1) coefficient is a nonzero polynomial (Lucas). | [Invariant thresholds in dimension 3](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-invariant-dimension-three) |
| `thm:cube-invariant-attainment-dimension-three` | On {0,1}^3 in characteristic != 2, whenever I^{(d+1)}_m != 0 its initial degree l_0 is attained by an S_4-invariant form, a nonzero multiple of prod_i D_{p_i} (balanced partition of the dimension-3 law); in characteristic != 2, 3 also l_0 = l_0^{S_3}; this is conj:cube-invariant-attainment for n = 3. | Working proof from lem:cube-boundary-generator-invariant, the product bound's lowest parts, the dimension-3 law and Reynolds averaging. | [Invariant thresholds in dimension 3](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-invariant-dimension-three) |
| `thm:cube-boundary-generator-invariant-all-n` | On {0,1}^n in characteristic 0, for every n >= 2 and d >= 1, the boundary threshold ideal I^{(d+1)}_N (N = N_{2,n}(d)) is principal, generated by W_N = Delta_{n,d}/g_{n,d} = c Delta^nc/g^nc, which is S_{n+1}-invariant and vanishes on no collision hyperplane; so l_0 at every boundary is attained by an invariant, and Delta^nc, g^nc are invariants too. | Working proof: rank-1 reflexive kernel, semi-invariance under the S_{n+1}-stable principal ideal, a sign-type semi-invariant vanishes on every mirror, and v_D(W_N) = v_D(Delta) - v_D(g) = 0 for every collision D (collision-exponent theorem). | [Boundary generator invariant](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-boundary-invariant) |
| `check:cube-dimension-four-row-d3` | On {0,1}^4 over F_32003 at savings 4: the S_4-invariant thresholds for m = 28..38 are 15, 13, 11, 10, 8, 7, 5, 4, 3, 2, 2 (0 at the order-zero threshold m = 39); no invariant solution of excess 0 or 1 has a nonzero top, so 2 <= l_0(4,m) <= these values, with equality under conj:cube-invariant-attainment. | Finite check by research/tools/bmd_cube_symmetric_solutions.cpp in its new fflas-ffpack rank mode, validated on the d = 2 row and the recorded d = 3 values at m = 35, 36, 38. | [Savings-4 row and monotone thresholds](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-row-d3) |
| `conj:cube-threshold-monotone` | On {0,1}^n over a field of characteristic != 2, l_0(h, m+1) <= l_0(h, m) for all h, m (l_0 = infinity when the ideal is 0); equivalently delta_F(n, k+1, l) <= delta_F(n, k, l) + 2. The savings form is false over F_2; the case n <= 3 is prop:cube-threshold-monotone-low-dimension. | Refuted in its full odd-characteristic scope by prop:cube-monotonicity-char-five-refutation: for every n>=4 over characteristic five the degree jumps by three from k=l+5 to l+6. The earlier n<=3 theorem is unaffected. | [Savings-4 row and monotone thresholds](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-row-d3) |
| `prop:cube-threshold-monotone-low-dimension` | On {0,1}^n with n <= 3 over every field of characteristic != 2, l_0(h, m+1) <= l_0(h, m) for all h, m; equivalently the savings are nondecreasing in k at fixed origin order (n = 1: savings m; n = 2: ceil(m/2); n = 3: B(d, rho) is nonincreasing in rho). | Working proof from the per-order laws for n = 1, 2 and the dimension-3 law, with a three-case analysis of B(d, rho); checked numerically for d <= 400. | [Savings-4 row and monotone thresholds](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-row-d3) |
| `thm:cube-order-zero-dimension-four-linear-bound` | On {0,1}^4 in characteristic 0 (and every odd characteristic except 5, 179, 281, 2959174039205819), the order-zero threshold M(d) (least m = k-1 with savings >= d+1 at origin order 0) satisfies M(d) <= 20d - 21 for every d >= 2, with M(1) = 5 and M(2) = 19 exactly in characteristic 0: products give M(d1+d2-1) <= M(d1) + M(d2) + 1, and an exact rational certificate gives M(2) <= 19. | Working proof: the product rule at origin order 0 and an exact rational solution of the symmetric order-zero system at d = 2, m = 19 (research/tools/bmd_cube_order_zero_exact.cpp, verified A x = b over Z), with exact unsolvability for m <= 18. | [Order zero is at most 20d - 21](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-order-zero-linear) |
| `ex:cube-order-zero-quadratic-false` | conj:cube-order-zero-dimension-four-quadratic (M(d) = 3d^2 + 5d - 3 on {0,1}^4 in characteristic 0) is false for every d >= 4, in characteristic 0 and in large odd characteristic: M(d) <= 20d - 21 < 3d^2 + 5d - 3, e.g. M(4) <= 59 < 65. | Refutation from thm:cube-order-zero-dimension-four-linear-bound; 3d^2 + 5d - 3 - (20d - 21) = 3(d-2)(d-3) > 0 for d >= 4. | [Order zero is at most 20d - 21](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-order-zero-linear) |
| `conj:cube-order-zero-dimension-four-linear` | On {0,1}^4 in characteristic 0, the order-zero threshold is M(d) = 20d - 21 for every d >= 2: products of the d = 2 order-zero witness are optimal. | Conjecture: upper bound proved (thm:cube-order-zero-dimension-four-linear-bound); equality exact in characteristic 0 for 2 <= d <= 4 (d = 3: check:cube-order-zero-dimension-four-thirty-nine; d = 4: check:cube-order-zero-dimension-four-fifty-nine; full-rank systems modulo a prime lifted to Q).  | [Order zero is at most 20d - 21](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-order-zero-linear) |
| `thm:cube-order-zero-rate` | On {0,1}^n over every field, with b_n(e) the least multiplicity k with savings >= e+n-2 at origin order 0: b_n is subadditive and nondecreasing, b_n(e) >= 2^{n-1} e, and if one b_n(e_0) is finite the limit c_n = lim b_n(e)/e = inf b_n(e)/e exists (Fekete), and the savings at every k are k/c_n + O(1) from above and k/c_n - o(k) from below; c_1 = 1, c_2 = 2, c_3 = 5 (characteristic != 2), 8 <= c_4 <= 20 (characteristic 0 and odd characteristic outside 5, 179, 281, 2959174039205819), and c_n = 2^{n-1} in characteristic 2. | Working proof: the product rule at origin order 0 (savings h_1 + h_2 - n + 2), the multiplicity Schwartz-Zippel bound, Fekete's lemma; values from the recorded per-order laws and the linear order-zero bound. | [Order-zero rate](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-order-zero-rate) |
| `lem:cube-triple-double-windows` | On {0,1}^4 in characteristic != 2, d >= 2, at the triple-double point P = (0,0,c,c) (c != 0), every solution W of the (d+1)-system satisfies: W(P) kills w^i, w = (1+4cT)^{1/2}, for -(4d-5) <= i <= 7d-7 and i = 4d (11d - 11 exponents for d >= 3, [-3, 8] for d = 2). | Working proof adapting lem:cube-double-point-windows: restriction to y_1 = 0, lifts along y_2 -> 0, the arc y_3 -> y_4 (window [-(4d-5), 4d-2] and 4d), and the Mobius transport to the frame with the pair at infinity (window [-(6d-7), 2d], transported to [-d, 7d-7]). | [Triple-double windows](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-triple-double-windows) |
| `thm:cube-order-zero-dimension-four-lower-bound` | On {0,1}^4 over every field of characteristic != 2: for d >= 3 and m <= 11d - 12 (m <= 11 for d = 2) every solution of the (d+1)-system vanishes at the ten triple-double points; hence l_0(d+1, m) >= 1, the order-zero threshold is M(d) >= 11d - 11, and the order-zero rate satisfies c_4 >= 11 (so 11 <= c_4 <= 20 in characteristic 0). | Working proof from lem:cube-triple-double-windows as in thm:cube-order-zero-value, with the S_5 symmetry and thm:cube-order-zero-rate. | [Triple-double windows](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-triple-double-windows) |
| `ex:cube-collision-windows-slope` | conj:cube-collision-regime-windows is false for every d >= 7 in its triple-double part: the triple-double points lie in V(I^{(d+1)}_m) for all m <= 11d - 12 > 10d - 6, so neither the maximal order 10d - 6 there nor the emptiness of V(I_m) for m >= 10d - 5 holds. | Refutation from thm:cube-order-zero-dimension-four-lower-bound; the fitted slope 10 agreed with 11d - 12 up to d = 6. | [Triple-double windows](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-triple-double-windows) |
| `lem:cube-order-zero-restriction` | On {0,1}^n over any field, for a linear subspace L of F^n let M_L(d) be the least m with an order-zero solution restricted to L (W_c in F[L] homogeneous of degree m - c, W_m = 1, all identities of V_{n,d} holding on L). Then M_L(d) <= M_{L'}(d) for L contained in L', and M_L(d) <= M(d). | Working proof: the identities of a solution hold on every subspace, and restriction preserves homogeneity and W_m = 1. For lines in dimension 3 essentially the order-zero case of lem:cube-line-restriction-bound; reviewed by a fresh-context referee. | [Order-zero restrictions](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-order-zero-restrictions) |
| `check:cube-order-zero-restrictions` | Over F_1000003, least m with a restricted order-zero solution: {0,1}^3 a random line 9, 14, 19 (= 5d - 1) for d = 2, 3, 4, collision lines 5, 7, 9; {0,1}^4 two random lines 17, 30, 42, three lines through a triple-double point 15-16, 27-28, 38-40, a line in y_1 = y_2 9, 14, 19, collision lines 5, 7, 9; {0,1}^4 two planes each 19 (d = 2) and 38 (d = 3), against the global 19 and 39 (F_1000003). | Finite check by modular linear algebra (FLINT and fflas-ffpack ranks) on random and special lines and planes, kernels validated on the whole space for n = 2, 3; F_1000003 only, solvability at fixed m not transferred to characteristic 0. | [Order-zero restrictions](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-09-26-cube-order-zero-restrictions) |
| `lem:cube-restriction-exactness` | For any degree-0 map A of graded free modules over F[y_1..y_n] (n >= 2), with K = ker A and C = coker A, and a nonzero linear form lambda: K/lambda K -> K_L = ker(A mod lambda) is injective with cokernel (0 :_C lambda)(-1), so K_L = K/lambda K iff lambda is a nonzerodivisor on C; if lambda lies in no associated prime of C other than the irrelevant ideal m, this holds iff m is not associated to C, and for n >= 3 iff depth K >= 3. For W_RS blocks of k+1 forms with all prefix patterns, y = (2,1,...,1) works; the core is row-free under the pullback hypotheses (cor:subfamily-row-freeness), so under those hypotheses (and a row-i-empty point with value y) the spread family, whose joint span contains r_i, fails at the family level for the forms as given. | Working proof for arbitrary clause systems. | `prop:pinned-lift-certificate` | Pinned lift certificate: (1) rows with rho_i = 0 on Q drop out of the lift conditions of prop:design-lift-criterion; (2) for a partial matching rho and a bipartite graph G' on the unmatched pigeons, the restriction set Q' = {rho u U : U a matching of G'} has 1 not in N_{D-1}(Q') and N_D(Q') cap F_{D-1} in N_{D-1}(Q') for every D <= B whenever the matching complexes M(G'[T]) have vanishing reduced homology in degree \|T\|-2 for 1 <= \|T\| <= B (lem:graph-matching-extension via the degree-exact matching basis of the hereditary set), so weak unary PHP plus any constraints vanishing on Q' has no degree-B refutation; (3) conditionally on that homology for the random left-5-regular G' of thm:cell-family-w at \|T\| <= 22k, the cell-family restriction set lies in the allowed set of the equivalent implication family and certifies W at 22k, where row freeness is not expected (confinement proved only for two columns): conditionally, the certificate is complete for these families in its lift form. | Working proof of (1) and (2) after a fresh-context review. Correction (28 September 2026, prop:blocked-centre-lift-failure): the homology hypothesis of (3) fails at blocked centres, typical in the residual (prop:spider-unfilled, prop:blocked-centre-unfilled), and the conclusion of (3) fails at 22k whenever the residual has a spider centre and h+1 > (110k-25) Delta; the restriction set is not a top-lift certificate. | [Pinned lift certificate](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-pinned-lift-certificate) |
| `prop:blocked-centre-lift-failure` | Blocked-centre lift failure: over any field, on the matching set of a bipartite graph (pinned pigeons allowed), if an unpinned pigeon r has N(r) = {h_1..h_d}, d >= 1, and distinct pigeons n_1..n_d, v_1..v_l other than r have holes n_i ~ h_i, p_i and v_j ~ a_j, b_j with all 2d+2l holes distinct, then f = prod x_{n_i h_i} prod x_{v_j a_j} lies in N_{d+l+1} cap F_{d+l} but not in N_{d+l} (a signed functional on the 2^{d+l} special matchings), so the top lift of prop:design-lift-criterion fails at D = d+l+1; hence the cell-family restriction set fails the lift at 22k whenever its residual has a spider centre and h+1 > (110k-25) Delta, correcting prop:pinned-lift-certificate (3). | `prop:lagged-lift-criterion` | Lagged lift criterion: over any field, in the setting of prop:design-lift-criterion, (1) if D <= D', N_{D'} cap F_{D-1} contained in N_{D'-1} and 1 not in N_{D'-1}, then V_D(Q) is contained in N_{D'} and 1 is not in V_D(Q), so weak unary PHP plus constraints vanishing on Q has no degree-D PC refutation (D' = D is the top lift); (2) with e(a,b) the number of elements of degree a and NS level b in a basis adapted to both flags, the top lift at D is sum_{a<D} e(a,D) = 0 and the lagged hypothesis is sum_{a<=D-1} e(a,D') = 0, so falls of depth b-a <= D'-D are harmless; (3) on filtered products with split rows the maximal depth up to a level is at most the factors' maximum (depth min(b-a, d-c) of u tensor w); (4) in the product model a coupled pair with any c0 (m = 2, 3) has no degree-D refutation when the other rows' factor lifts in every degree through D+2. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; part (4) uses the finite check ex:coupled-pair-fall-depths. | [Lagged lift criterion](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-lagged-lift) |
| `ex:coupled-pair-fall-depths` | Coupled-pair fall depths: in the value space Y = {y != 0} x {y' != 0} x states of prop:single-row-lift-transfer, for m = 2, 3, the fall table through level 8 (complete, since functions on Y have degree <= 5) has only e(2,3) = m-1 for c0 = 0, e(1,3) = 1 and e(2,3) = m-1 for c0 = 2, and no falls for c0 = 1; 1 never enters N^Y; the control {y != 0} x F_3 has no falls. So coupled pairs fall by at most two degrees. | `conj:lagged-lift-subset` | Lagged-lift subset (conjecture): in the setting of conj:top-lift-subset, with high probability some nonempty subset Q of the allowed set of some equivalent family has N_{D'}(Q) cap F^Q_{D-1} contained in N_{D'-1}(Q) and 1 not in N_{D'-1}(Q) for some D' <= cD, c an absolute constant; by prop:lagged-lift-criterion it gives W_RS at degree D; implied by conj:top-lift-subset (D' = D); coupled pairs in normal form satisfy it with D' = D+2 in the product model with m = 2, 3 when the other rows' factor lifts through D+2, and blocked configurations (depth 1) do not obstruct it; the truncated support Q_D is untested. | Conjecture: the route's weakest recorded certificate statement; no gluing theorem in lagged form is known. | [Lagged lift criterion](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-lagged-lift) |
| `prop:expander-fall-bound` | Expander fall bound: over any field, for functional graph PHP on an (s,delta)-boundary expander of maximum left degree d with D_0 = floor(delta s/(2d)) >= d, on the matching set (pinned pigeons allowed) every f of degree a <= D_0 with a PC derivation of degree <= D_0 (in particular f in N_{D_0}) lies in N_{a + floor(da/delta)}: R(f) = 0 for Miksa-Nordstrom's operator, t - R(t) lies in I_E(Sup_s(t)) with \|Sup_s(t)\| <= d deg t/delta, and on matchings g = -sum_{S nonempty} g prod_{u in S} rho_u. Hence depths <= floor(da/delta) below D_0; the lagged lift holds at (D, D') for D-1+floor(d(D-1)/delta)+1 <= D' <= D_0; the cell-family restriction set is a lagged-lift certificate at D when 6D-5 <= floor(s/10); and with constraints only required to lie in N_{D'}(Q), sparse and row-sparse residual clauses are covered when 6D <= floor(s/10). | Working proof, given the imported Miksa-Nordstrom theorem, after a fresh-context review. | [Expander fall bound](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-expander-lagged-lift) |
| `lem:row-count-depth-bound` | Row-count depth bound: over F_p, on a finite point set with a degree filtration (degree of a product at most the sum) and rows rho_1..rho_m of degree <= 1 with N_b = sum_i rho_i F_{b-1}, if f in F_a vanishes on the common zeros of the rows in T then f is in N_{a+(p-1)\|T\|} (expand f(1 - prod_{i in T}(1 - rho_i^{p-1}))); so falls certified by tau rows have depth <= (p-1)tau, single-row value spaces (any number of coupled pairs on one row) fall by at most p-1, and the lagged lift holds at (D, D') when every element of N_{D'} cap F_{D-1} is a sum of degree-(D-1) elements certified by at most tau rows with (p-1)tau <= D'-D. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Lagged route review](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-lagged-route-review) |
| `prop:single-degree-taylor-lift` | Single-degree Taylor lift: over F_3, in the setting of thm:based-taylor-glue (base with Booleanity generators, product constraints with factors L-a or chi_a(L)), fix one degree D; if the base is z-injective at D (V_D cap P_{<=D-1} = V_{D-1}) and the degree-D signed top syzygies are spanned by the Frobenius and coherent-pair syzygies, then V'_D cap P_{<=D-1} is contained in V'_{D-1} (no fall at level D), and if also 1 is not in V'_{D-1} the PC closure through D lies in V'_D and there is no PC refutation of degree D. So A3's Tor vanishing through 22k may be replaced by Taylor generation at any single degree D' >= 22k where the weak base is z-injective, plus a Nullstellensatz design at D'-1. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; a refinement of thm:based-taylor-glue (one degree of Taylor generation and z-injectivity, with the design one degree lower assumed). | [Single-degree Taylor lift](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-single-degree-taylor) |
| `prop:exact-taylor-propagation` | Exact Taylor propagation: over any field, in the setting of thm:taylor-propagation and prop:lift-obstruction (Frobenius elements lifted), adding a column c gives Def_e(R') = dim ker ob_c + \|c\| Def_{e-1}(R) - rank(delta-bar_c), where delta_v sends a relation sum g_i (x) x_i among Taylor generators (formal combinations with sum g_i x_i = 0) to sum (d_v g'_i) x_i in Syz_{e-1}(R) and delta-bar_c collects these modulo T_{e-1}(R); no clean lower degree is assumed, and the clean case is prop:lift-obstruction. For product tops over F_3 the derivatives are linear in the new coefficients with components fixed on R, so with calA_{e-1}(R) their span on relations, Def_e(R') >= \|c\| dim(Syz_{e-1}(R)/(T_{e-1}(R) + calA_{e-1}(R))) for every added column: lower classes outside calA reappear once per new cell. | Working proof after a fresh-context review. | [Exact Taylor propagation](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-exact-taylor-propagation) |

| `prop:sparse-failure-sets` | Sparse failure sets: over F_3 on the weak unary base (B = collision-free 0/1 points, m = N+1), for near-refutations Lambda = sum b_i (r_i - 1), deg b_i <= D-1, with failure sets Phi = {Lambda != 1}: (1) E contains a degree-D failure set iff E meets the support of every degree-D point design; (2) failure sets are closed under intersection with degrees adding (Lambda_1 + Lambda_2 - Lambda_1 Lambda_2), and -Lambda_1 - Lambda_2 has failure set inside the union at the larger degree; (3) for F in F_3[y_J] of degree d with F(1..1) = 1, 1 - F(r_J) has failure set {F(r_J) != 0} at degree d, e.g. {r_i != 0 for i in J} at degree \|J\|; (4) under the uniform measure on B that set has density <= (1 - e^{-1})^{\|J\|} < 0.633^{\|J\|} (negative association of bin occupancies), below 0.16^t < 3^{-t} at D >= 4t+2; (5) for N - r >= 3 and D <= floor((N-r+1)/2) every failure set has >= (N)_r points (restricted matching designs with disjoint supports); (6) under W_RS Pr[Phi inside E] <= M 3^{-t} for each fixed Phi, attained by the row-residue block L_1 = r_{i0} - 1, L_l = r_{il}, refuted at NS degree 4t+2 exactly when C e_1 = 0. | `prop:joint-absorption-rank` | Joint absorption rank: in the setting of prop:exact-taylor-propagation with product tops over F_3 in one fixed list of F distinct forms (standing hypothesis, as in prop:column-configuration-defect), adding a column c with coefficient matrix L_c (\|c\| x F, rank r_c), U = Syz_{e-1}(R)/T_{e-1}(R) and Psi-bar = (Psi-bar_f)_f : Rel_e(R) -> U^F the classes of the coefficient components of derivatives of relations among Taylor generators: (1) delta-bar_c = (L_c tensor id_U) o Psi-bar; (2) Def_e(R') = dim ker ob_c + (\|c\| Def_{e-1}(R) - rank delta-bar_c), both terms nonnegative, so Def_e(R') = 0 iff ker ob_c = 0 and delta-bar_c is onto U^c; (3) Def_e(R') >= (\|c\| - r_c) Def_{e-1}(R) (the one-column term of prop:column-configuration-defect) and Def_e(R') >= \|c\| Def_{e-1}(R) - rank Psi-bar, so with a positive lower defect Taylor generation after the column needs r_c = \|c\| and rank Psi-bar >= \|c\| Def_{e-1}(R), a necessary condition independent of calA = U (neither implies the other). On the weak base (\|c\| = m) single-degree Taylor generation is a staircase of lower-degree conditions for low-rank columns and needs m-fold joint absorption for full-rank ones. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; a necessary condition, with no mechanism supplying it for dense families. | [Joint absorption rank](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-joint-absorption-rank) |
| `prop:nontrivial-relation-bound` | Nontrivial relation bound: in the setting of prop:joint-absorption-rank (product tops over F_3 on the square-free board algebra, Frobenius generators L^{3-eps} e_b, Koszul pairs), the derivative map Psi-bar vanishes on the span Triv_e(R) of monomial multiples of commutations of Frobenius generators of one top, self-annihilations L^eps (x) L^{3-eps} e_b (L^3 = 0 in characteristic 3), Frobenius-Koszul relations and Koszul triples; so rank Psi-bar <= h_e(R) = dim Rel_e(R)/Triv_e(R), and with a positive lower defect Taylor generation after a column c needs h_e(R) >= \|c\| Def_{e-1}(R), while Def_e(R') >= \|c\| Def_{e-1}(R) - h_e(R) for every column. | `conj:relation-excess-universality` | Relation excess universality (conjecture): over F_3, for independent random product tops on the square-free board algebra of an m x N board, at multiplier degrees below the fill point, the nontrivial relation count h_e = dim Rel_e/Triv_e among Taylor generators behaves like the rank deficiency of a random F_3 matrix of the same shape: bounded in probability with Pr[h_e >= k] <= C 3^{-c k^2}; the relation-level analogue of conj:product-top-cohen-lenstra. Consequence (proved from it with prop:nontrivial-relation-bound): on the weak base (\|c\| = m) h_e < m and Def_{e-1} >= 1 force Def_e(R') > 0, so single-degree Taylor generation for random dense tops requires the staircase Def_{e-j} = 0 on every board with j columns deleted and gains nothing from absorption. | `prop:relative-covering` | Relative covering: over F_3 for weak unary PHP plus a W_RS family with full-rank prefixes C_b (rank t), excluded sets E_b = {g_b != 0, C_b g_b = 0}, and kappa_b(w) = max over codimension-t subspaces V of w{g_b in V minus 0} for a probability weight w: (1) a degree-D failure set inside E forces sum_b w(Phi cap E_b) >= 1 for every weight w on Phi; (2) if every degree-D failure set carries a weight with sum_b kappa_b < 1, there is no degree-D Nullstellensatz refutation for any full-rank prefixes (via prop:failure-set-criterion); (3) aligned kernels {p_j1 = ... = p_jt = 0} give kappa_b >= w{those t forms nonzero} - w{g_b = 0}, about (2/3)^t under independent zero statuses, so the all-prefix form needs t > log_{3/2} M, W's prefix length (W_RS's degree bound stays <= 44t); (4) row-residue blocks and the common-prefix hole family violate the hypothesis, as they must. The hypothesis is a pseudorandomness property of failure sets, unproved. | Working proof of a reduction after a fresh-context review; its hypothesis on failure sets is open. | [Relative covering](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-relative-covering) |
| `prop:cylinder-spread` | Cylinder spread: over F_3 on the weak unary base with the uniform product measure on B, let the column damping of a block be eps_b = max over nonzero combinations l_a of its forms and shifts beta in F_3^m of \|E_B omega^{l_a + beta.r}\| (a product over columns of \|1 + sum_i omega^{alpha_iu}\|/(m+1)). (1) Under the uniform weight on a residue cylinder Y = {r_J in R}, R containing (1..1), \|J\| = j, every nonzero combination has bias <= 3^{j/2}(e^2(1+2/N))^j eps_b, and kappa_b <= (2/3)^t + 3^{h_b/2} times that bias (pivot bound (2/3)^t for codimension-t subspaces under independent Bernoulli(1/3) statuses). (2) If M(2/3)^t <= 1/2 and 3^{h_b/2}(bias) < 1/(2M) for all blocks, no full-rank prefixes cover Y (prop:relative-covering), so no failure set containing a residue cylinder lies in E; this includes residue-cylinder failure sets and every near-refutation omitting a row equation (its failure set contains the N! perfect matchings of the other rows). (3) Independent uniform coefficients give eps_b <= (m+1)^{-N/4} with probability >= 1 - 3^{h_b+m}(m+1)^{-N/2}, enough for every depth when h_b <= N and N >= N_0(K). (4) Row-residue and column-statistic forms have little or no damping. Remaining: near-refutations using every row. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; settles failure sets containing residue cylinders, not near-refutations using every row. | [Cylinder spread](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-cylinder-spread) |
| `prop:junta-residue-spread` | Junta-residue spread: over F_3 on the weak unary base with the uniform measure on B, for a junta-residue set Y = {x_U = sigma, r(x) in R} (d = \|U\| columns with fixed states, R in F_3^m) with conditional probability p(Y) = Pr[r in R \| x_U = sigma], and damping away from d columns eps_b^(d): (1) every nonzero combination of a block's forms has bias <= \|\|hat f_R\|\|_1 eps_b^(d)/p(Y) under the uniform weight on Y (the column conditioning cancels), so kappa_b <= (2/3)^t + 3^{h_b/2} times that, and if M(2/3)^t <= 1/2 and M 3^{h_b/2}\|\|hat f_R\|\|_1 eps_b^(d) < p(Y)/2 no full-rank prefixes cover Y or any failure set containing it; (2) random dense blocks have eps_b^(d) <= (m+1)^{-(N-d)/4} w.h.p. for all d <= N/2 at once, enough for h_b <= N, d <= N/2, p(Y) >= (m+1)^{-N/16}, large N; (3) residue near-refutations Lambda = F(r) have junta-residue failure sets; (4) for every near-refutation the uniform weight on its failure set has bias <= (2/3)(eps_b + eta(Lambda))/Pr[Phi], eta = max \|E omega^{l_a +- Lambda}\|, so it is spread unless Lambda correlates with a damped linear phase or omega^Lambda is strongly biased. | `prop:junta-residue-classes` | Junta-residue classes: over F_3 on the weak unary base with the uniform measure on B, for a nonempty class Y = {x_U = sigma, r(x) = rho} (d = \|U\| columns fixed, one residue vector): (1) Pr[r = rho \| x_U = sigma] >= (5e(N+2)/N')^{-N'}/2 with N' = N - d, at least 30^{-N}/2 for d <= N/2 and N >= 20 (counts from {0,1,2} bumped by 3 to fill the columns); (2) hence, by prop:junta-residue-spread with the single-class Fourier norm 1, for random dense families (h_b <= N) at W's prefix length and N >= N_0(K) (of order 10^5 to 10^8 with the second-moment damping bound), no full-rank prefixes cover a failure set containing a nonempty junta-residue class with d <= N/2, and every residue near-refutation F(r) with nonempty failure set is uncovered; (3) on a class a near-refutation equals P_Y = sum_i (rho_i - 1) b_i restricted, of degree <= D-1, and Y lies in the failure set iff P_Y omits 1; (4) degree-two near-refutations sum_i (c_i + L_i)(r_i - 1) with damped L_i have no such core, the first core-free case. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; the core-free correlated case remains open. | [Junta-residue classes](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-junta-residue-classes) |
| `prop:density-transfer` | Density transfer: over F_3 on the weak unary base, for a failure set Phi and a nonempty junta-residue class Y with density delta_Y = Pr_Y[Phi]: (1) kappa_b(unif on Phi cap Y) <= kappa_b(unif_Y)/delta_Y, so if sum_b kappa_b(unif_Y) < delta_Y no full-rank prefixes cover Phi; for random dense families this holds at prefix length t >= log_{3/2}(4M/delta_Y); (2) degree-two near-refutations sum_i (c_i + L_i)(r_i - 1) with damped multipliers have delta_Y >= 4/9 on every class (0.6 for random multipliers at large N) and are never covered at t >= log_{3/2}(9M) (log_{3/2}(7M) for random multipliers); (3) if Phi(Lambda) lies in {prod_{k in S} L_k != 0}, then 1 = Lambda + gamma * gamma(1 - Lambda) (gamma = prod L_k, gamma^2 = 1 off its zeros) is a Nullstellensatz refutation of weak PHP plus gamma of degree D + 2\|S\|, excluded by lem:member-pinning for row-independent forms under its board hypotheses; (4) a covered failure set must be thin in every class (density below 4M(2/3)^t), contain no junta-residue class, and not be exactly aligned with a product of few row-independent forms. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; approximately aligned thin failure sets remain open. | [Density transfer](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-density-transfer) |
| `prop:thinness-equivalence` | Thinness equivalence: over F_3 on the weak unary base with W_RS blocks, full-rank prefixes C_b and excluded set E = union of E_b = {g_b != 0, C_b g_b = 0}: (1) for every set Y of positive measure and all full-rank prefixes Pr_Y[E] <= sum_b kappa_b(unif_Y), so a failure set inside E has density at most that sum in Y; (2) the conclusions of prop:density-transfer (1), prop:junta-residue-classes (2), prop:cylinder-spread (2) and prop:junta-residue-spread (1) are instances of (1), using the failure set only through its density; (3) Phi inside E_b forces the pattern span W_b(Phi) into ker C_b (dim w <= h_b - t); a fixed W lies in the kernel of a uniform full-rank C_b with probability >= 0.56 * 3^{-tw}, and at least 2^{w(h_b-w)} w-dimensional subspaces are spanned by 0/1 vectors, so a union bound over pattern spans does not converge when h_b - w >= t log_2 3, which kills the planned union over alignment types; (4) the damping bounds control kappa_b only when N - d > 2 ln3 h_b / ln(m+1) (about 2.2N/ln N free columns at h_b = N), while restricted matching designs live on as few as 2D - 1 free columns. | Working proof after a fresh-context review; a correction of framing for the Nullstellensatz line of A1, whose remaining question sits at few free columns. | [Thinness equivalence](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/odd-prime-reslin-php/#entry-2026-09-28-thinness-equivalence) |
