Corollary: if P = F(t^N - s) on a closed annulus K with F, s zero-free, \|t s'/s\| < N on K, \|s\| < r2^N on the outer and \|s\| > r1^N on the inner circle, then P has exactly N - wind(s) zeros in K, all simple. | Working proof: direct differentiation at a zero and the argument principle. | [Log-derivative criterion](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-far-logderivative-criterion) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-coefficient-cut-blocks` | Hypothesis (refuted): on each long Newton edge [m1, m2] of P(t) = (1-t)^d W_(b-1)(t/(1-t)), the mid-edge cut A = P mod t^c, B = P div t^c (c = floor((m1+m2)/2)) satisfies (sup\|tA'/A - m1\| + sup\|tB'/B - (m2-c)\|)/(m2-m1) < 1 on the band \|log\|t\| - log r\| <= pi/L, which with lem:far-logderivative-criterion would make all roots on the circle simple. | Refuted at e = 4..11: the ratio is between 1.86 and 15.3 on all 96 tested circles, not decreasing in e (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_block_logderiv.gp, research/results/bmd-20261003-zzp/block-logderiv-2.txt). | [Log-derivative criterion](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-far-logderivative-criterion) |
| `conj:cube-last-far-log-radii` | For every e, the slopes -u_0 > ... > -u_3 of the four long Newton edges of P(t) = (1-t)^d W_(b-1)(t/(1-t)) satisfy N u_i = c_i log N + d_i + o(1) (N = R_e + 7/2) with equal consecutive differences c_(i+1) - c_i: the far-root circles lie at distance Theta(log N/N) from \|t\| = 1, with log-radii in arithmetic progression of step about 4.1 log N/N. | Conjecture: at e = 4..11 the fits N u_i = c_i log N + d_i have c ~ (-6.72, -2.65, 1.52, 5.61) (with a 1/e term: -6.72, -2.55, 1.52, 5.71) and residuals <= 0.021, while e u = C + D/e, N u = a sqrt(e) + b and a N^(1/4) + b fit far worse (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_log_radii.py, research/results/bmd-20261003-zzq/log-radii.txt); equal differences hold to about +-0.1. | [Last far log radii](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-last-far-log-radii) |

| `lem:cube-last-far-frobenius-shift` | For every e and odd prime p > d = R_(e+2), q = (p-1)/2: W_(F_p)(V_p) = (x^3(1+x)^3)^d prod kappa_i^(-1) (W(F_(b-1)) mod p), V_p = x^3(1+x)^3 P_<n + x^3 + (1+x)^3 + x^3(1+x)^q P_<4e + x^q(1+x)^3 P_<4e + x^q(1+x)^(q+1) P_<4 (half-integral exponents shifted by p/2); so (W(F) = C x^alpha (1+x)^beta W_(b-1), W_(b-1) primitive, v_p(C) >= 0) W(V_p) = 0 iff v_p(C) > 0, and otherwise the far parts of W(V_p) and W_(b-1) mod p are proportional. | Working proof: x^(p/2), (1+x)^(p/2) are constants in characteristic p and the Wronskian is multilinear; exact check at e = 1, 2, 3 (14 primes above the window proportional with full degree; window primes below 2n+8e+7 give W(V_p) = 0; p = 2n+8e+7 = 17, 61 proportional) (research/tools/bmd_cube_last_far_frobenius_shift.gp, research/results/bmd-20261003-zzy/frobenius-shift.txt). | [Last far Frobenius shift](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-03-cube-last-far-frobenius-shift) |

Hence (B) at N (N >= 5) holds if some interior configuration D0 attaining T(b), with holomorphic non-branch part W_D (constant branch exponents and degree), has no root at a branch value and, for every root of multiplicity >= 3 of W_(D0), some configuration derivative d_v W(z0) != 0. | Working proof: rescaling with Rouche and Hurwitz near each root, a common direction outside finitely many hyperplanes, multiplicity <= 2 preserved, no roots from infinity, openness of attainment (cited); analogous to lem:cube-far-first-order-splitting at interior configurations. | [Base deformation splitting](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-base-deformation-splitting) |
| `conj:cube-middle-far-ore-separable` | For every even-peeling middle step 2 <= k <= b-2 there is a collapse prime p with v_p(W_k(0)) = 1, all residual polynomials of the Newton polygon of W_k(y-1) at p separable (observed: a staircase of height-1 sides with lengths mostly increasing by 2), and non-branch multiplicity <= 2; by Dumas and Ore this certifies that W_k has roots of multiplicity <= 2. | Conjecture: at l = 2 ((b,k) = (6,4), (7,5), (8,6)) all 37 collapse primes have separable residual polynomials at -1 (6-8 sides, as many as v_p(W(-1)); two sides of height 2) (research/tools/bmd_cube_middle_far_ore.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-f/middle-ore.txt). | [Middle far Ore staircase](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-middle-far-ore-staircase) |
| `conj:cube-middle-far-branch-count` | For every middle even-peeling step (l >= 2) and primes p in an upper window of the collapse range, the pivot minors at 0, -1, infinity are p-adic units, v_p(W_k(0)/lc) = 1 and v_p(W_k(-1)/lc) = c(l) (c(2) = 6), both arising only from Vandermonde pairs of local exponents at distance p/2. | Conjecture: \|W(0)/lc\| = \|L_0/L_oo\| and \|W(-1)/lc\| = \|L_-1/L_oo\| hold exactly at (b,k) = (6,4), (7,5), (8,6); at the upper collapse primes (61..83, 97..127, 137..173) minors are units and the valuations are 1 and 6 from Vandermonde pairs; lower primes have p in the minors (research/tools/bmd_cube_middle_far_branch_values.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-g/middle-branch-values.txt). | [Middle far branch count](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-middle-far-branch-count) |
| `conj:cube-far-layer-count` | For every even-peeling step (e, l) with e large enough relative to l, there is a run of primes p just above d = R_e+1+R_l+4e+4l+4el at which all pivot minors at 0, -1, infinity are p-adic units, v_p(L_0/L_oo) = 1 and v_p(L_-1/L_oo) = R_l = l(2l-1); hence v_p(W_k(0)/lc) = 1 and v_p(W_k(-1)/lc) = R_l. | Conjecture: holds at (e,l) = (3,1) p = 47..61, (3,2) 67..83, (3,3) 97..109, (4,3) 137..157 with unit minors; at (2,4) no run above d (valuations <= 18 < 28) (research/tools/bmd_cube_middle_far_branch_values.gp scan mode, research/results/bmd-20261004-h/layer-scan.txt). | [Far layer count](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-layer-count) |
| `lem:cube-far-layer-count` | For every even-peeling step (e, l) with the generic local exponent sets (E) of its far component (I_0 = [-R_l-2,-3] u [0,R_e+4e], H_0 = [4e-4el-7/2, 4e+4l-9/2], I_-1 = {-3} u [0,M-1], H_-1 = -7/2+[0,4e+4l-1], I_oo = [-(R_e-1),0] u [3,R_l+4l+3], H_oo = 9/2-4e+[0,4el+4e-1], M = R_e+R_l+4el) and every prime p > d with Q_lo = max(M+3-4e-4l, 4el+3, R_l+4l+4e-1) <= (p-1)/2 <= R_e+4el+3: N_0 - N_oo = 1 and N_-1 - N_oo = R_l, so with unit pivot minors and p not dividing lc, v_p(W_k(0)) = 1 (Eisenstein cluster at 0) and v_p(W_k(-1)) = R_l. | Working proof by interval counting (Step 2 of the Eisenstein proposition generalized); (E) checked exactly at seven (e, l) and the window matches all scanned valuations (research/tools/bmd_cube_middle_far_branch_values.gp sets and scan modes, research/results/bmd-20261004-i/exponent-sets.txt, research/results/bmd-20261004-h/layer-scan.txt). | [Far layer count lemma](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-layer-count-lemma) |
| `lem:cube-far-pivot-minors` | For every even-peeling step (e, l) the six pivot minors of the far component at 0, -1, infinity are, in absolute value, beta(C,s) = \|V(C)\| prod \|c^(falling s)\| / prod (s+i)! for explicit sets C (integral at 0: {-3} u {-7/2+j}_(j<4e), s = R_e; half at -1: {1/2-4l+j}_(j<4l), s = 4e-1; integral at oo: {-3} u {-5/2+j}_(j<4l), s = R_l; half at oo: {-7/2+j}_(j<4e), s = 4el), \|V(C_-1)\| / prod_(i<M) i! (integral at -1), and the box product prod_(i<4l) \|binom(-5/2+i, s)\| / binom(s+i, s), s = 4e+4l-4 (half at 0); all are nonzero, so the exponent sets (E) of lem:cube-far-layer-count hold. In its window all six are p-adic units for l >= 3 and for l = 2, e <= 2; for l = 2, e >= 3 only the integral minor at -1 can fail, with valuation 2 at p = 4e^2+6e+3 and 1 at p = 4e^2+6e+5. | Working proof by unitriangular reduction to two determinant identities (falling-factorial Vandermonde and the box formula) and prime bounds; exact checks of all six forms at twelve (e, l) and the predicted exceptions 241 (valuation 2), 383 and 653 (research/tools/bmd_cube_middle_far_branch_values.gp minors mode, research/results/bmd-20261004-j/). | [Far pivot minors](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-pivot-minors) |
| `cor:cube-far-branch-valuations` | For every even-peeling step (e, l) and every prime p > d with Q_lo <= (p-1)/2 <= R_e+4el+3 (the window of lem:cube-far-layer-count) and p not dividing lc(W_k), excluding p in {2R_e+1, 2R_e+3, 2R_e+5} when l = 1: v_p(W_k(0)) = 1 (Eisenstein cluster at 0); if moreover p is not 4e^2+6e+3 or 4e^2+6e+5 when l = 2, then v_p(W_k(-1)) = R_l. | Working proof: lem:cube-far-pivot-minors supplies (E) and unit minors for lem:cube-far-layer-count. | [Far pivot minors](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-pivot-minors) |
| `lem:cube-far-chain-reduction` | For an even-peeling far step (e, l), normalized c = 1, and m = R_l, let T_j be the non-branch part of the far Wronskian with A-block exponents -(j+2)..-3 and the other classes unchanged (so T_m = W_k), and Q_A the swapped Wronskian of lem:cube-far-first-order-splitting. Crum's identity gives T_(m-1) T_(m+1) = const x^s (1+x)^t [x(1+x)(T_m Q_A' - T_m' Q_A) + ((a_Q-a_m)(1+x) + (c_Q-c_m)x) T_m Q_A] (s, t integers), so gcd(T_m, T_(m-1) T_(m+1)) = 1 implies gcd(W_k, Q_A) = 1; if moreover G_A is linearly independent of G_B, G_C as functions of D, the first-order criterion holds at every multiple root of W_k. | Working proof from Crum's Wronskian identity and lem:cube-far-first-order-splitting; identity checked exactly modulo 2^61-1 at (e,l) = (1,2),(2,2),(1,3),(3,2),(2,3) (research/tools/bmd_cube_far_chain_coprime.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-k/chain-coprime.txt). | [Far chain review](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-chain-review) |
| `conj:cube-far-chain-coprime` | For every even-peeling step (e, l) with l >= 2 and m = R_l, the A-chain Wronskian T_m (= W_k) is coprime to T_(m-1) and to T_(m+1). | Conjecture: all gcds trivial modulo 2^61-1 at (e,l) = (1,2),(2,2),(1,3),(3,2),(2,3); no three-term recurrence, Adler-Moser-type companion identity or resultant product formula found (research/results/bmd-20261004-k/chain-coprime.txt, chain-tests.txt). | [Far chain review](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-chain-review) |
| `lem:cube-far-derivative-ladder` | For an even-peeling far step (e, l), c = 1, y = 1/x and Psi = y^-3 U (U the non-A classes, dim k), m >= 2: dim Psi^(j) = k for all j (monodromy), and off {0,-1,inf}, T_j has the roots of Wr_y(Psi^(j)) (j >= 1) and Q_A those of Wr_y(y, Psi^(m-1)); at a root r of T_m with T_(m-1)(r) != 0, mult_r T_m = ord_r(f_0 - 1) - k and Q_A(r) = 0 iff f_1^(k)(r) = 0 (adapted basis of Psi^(m-1)); if moreover mult_r T_m >= 3 and Q_A(r) = 0 then mult_r T_(m+1) >= 3. Hence (with independent G's, l >= 2) the first-order criterion fails at r only if T_(m-1)(r) = 0 or r is a root of multiplicity >= 3 of both T_m and T_(m+1). | Working proof by the derivative identity Wr(1..y^(j-1), g) = prod i! Wr(g^(j)), adapted bases and weights; y-side control at nine (e, l, m) (research/tools/bmd_cube_far_chain_coprime.gp ladder mode, research/results/bmd-20261004-l/ladder.txt). | [Far derivative ladder](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-derivative-ladder) |
| `lem:cube-far-ga-asymmetry` | In the first-order splitting of the even peeling (l >= 2, w_s = 1/D_s): each G_X depends only on the span of class X, so G_B and G_C are symmetric in w; if G_A is not invariant under some permutation of the w_s then G_A is not in span(G_B, G_C) and the first-order criterion holds at every root r of W_k with Q_A(r) != 0; for a class with consecutive pivots, G = (1/n) d/du log(W/u^N) at u = 0; at l = 2, G_A = -(11 w_1 + 13 w_2)/3. | Working proof (span uniqueness, multilinear Wronskian expansion with Vandermonde ratio n, branch exponents and degree count at l = 2); symbolic and exact checks (research/tools/bmd_cube_far_ga_symmetry.gp, research/results/bmd-20261004-m/). | [First-order coefficients](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-ga-asymmetry) |
| `conj:cube-far-ga-asymmetric` | For every l >= 2 the first-order coefficient G_A of the l-level class A is not symmetric under w_1 <-> w_2. | Conjecture: proved at l = 2; exact asymmetry at w_s = (2s+1)/(s+3) for l = 2, 3, 4, 5 (research/results/bmd-20261004-m/ga-asymmetry.txt). | [First-order coefficients](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-ga-asymmetry) |
| `lem:cube-far-sector-decomposition` | On the derivative ladder (y = 1/x, Psi = y^-3 U), at r not in {0,-1} every Taylor coefficient of each of the 4e mixed rows y^(3/2-4e+j)(1+y)^(-7/2) splits exactly as I_0(N) + I_-1(N) (keyhole integrals around rays from 0 and -1, endpoint circles included), while pure rows keep their Taylor sequences; hence Wr_y(Psi^(m))(r) = prod (m+s)! sum over subsets S of the mixed rows of the Casorati determinants D_S, grouped into 4e+1 sector sums by \|S\|. | Working proof: decay O(\|y\|^-3) of the mixed rows at infinity, contour deformation and multilinearity in the mixed rows. | [Far sector decomposition](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-sector-decomposition) |
| `conj:cube-far-sector-circles` | For fixed e and l -> infinity, all but O_e(l) roots of the far polynomial W_k = T_(R_l) lie in 4e annuli \|log\|1+x\| - log rho_i\| = O_e(1/R_l), each with R_l + O_e(1) roots, and these roots are simple. | Conjecture from the sector decomposition and Darboux heuristics; exact roots at (e,l) = (1,3), (1,4) show bands of 27 (one circle, R_4 = 28), 67 (two merged) and 32 roots, but bands far wider than O(1/R_l) at these sizes (research/results/bmd-20261004-n/sector-roots.txt). | [Far sector decomposition](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-far-sector-decomposition) |
| `lem:cube-far-x-sector-decomposition` | For every even-peeling step, with F the far blocks other than P_<R_e(x) (dim k' = 1+R_l+4e+4l+4el) and n = R_e: off {0,-1,inf} W_k has the same roots, with multiplicity, as Wr_x(F^(n)) = prod (n+s)! det[c_(i,n+s)(r)] (F contains no polynomial, by monodromy characters); the rows singular at both 0 and -1 are the 4l functions (1+x)^(-5/2) x^(1/2-4l+j); for non-real r, with cuts the rays from -1 and 0 pointing away from r, each splits exactly as c_N = I_0(N) + I_-1(N), so det[c] = sum_(s=0)^(4l) E_s, E_s summing the determinants with s mixed rows taking their I_0 parts. | Working proof: classical derivative identity, monodromy characters, decay O(\|x\|^-3) of mixed rows, contour deformation and multilinearity; numerically sum E_s = det[c] vanishes at the roots of W_(b-1) to 1e-100 and the split I_0 + I_-1 = c holds to 1.7e-29 (research/results/bmd-20261004-p/x-sector-balance.txt). | [Last-step sector balance](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-balance) |
| `conj:cube-far-x-sector-balance` | For every e >= 2, all but O(e) non-real roots r of the last-step far polynomial W_(b-1) satisfy, with the cuts of lem:cube-far-x-sector-decomposition: for some i in {0,1,2,3}, determined by the circle and increasing as \|t\| = \|x/(1+x)\| decreases, \|E_s(r)\| <= eps_e max(\|E_i(r)\|, \|E_(i+1)(r)\|) for s not in {i, i+1}, with eps_e -> 0, where E_s are the x-side sector sums. | Conjecture: at e = 4, 38 of 48 sampled non-real roots balance consecutive sums with third/largest <= 2.5e-4 (pairs (0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,4) on log\|t\| in [0.46,0.64], [0.07,0.15], [-0.33,-0.24], [-0.80,-0.60]); 10 others, against 22 = 8e-10 roots outside the four circles; at e = 2, 7 of 13; split validated to 1e-29 (research/results/bmd-20261004-p/x-sector-balance.txt). | [Last-step sector balance](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-balance) |
| `lem:cube-far-balance-certificate` | If T = E_i + E_(i+1) + R near a root r of T, all analytic with E_i(r) E_(i+1)(r) != 0, phi = E_(i+1)/E_i, and \|E_i(r)\| \|(log phi)'(r)\| > \|R(r)\| \|E_(i+1)'/E_(i+1)(r)\| + \|R'(r)\|, then r is a simple root; in particular with \|R\| <= eps\|E_i\|, \|R'\| <= eps N \|E_i\|/\|r(1+r)\|, \|E_(i+1)'/E_(i+1)\| <= C N/\|r(1+r)\| and \|r(1+r)(log phi)'\| >= delta N it holds once eps(C+1) < delta. | Working proof: T'(r) = -E_i (log phi)' - R E_(i+1)'/E_(i+1) + R' at the root. | [Last-step sector ratio](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-ratio) |
| `conj:cube-far-x-sector-ratio` | At the last even-peeling step, at all but O(1) of the roots where consecutive x-side sector sums E_i, E_(i+1) balance, kappa_i = r(1+r) d/dr log(E_(i+1)/E_i) = -(R_e + 7/2) + lambda_i with \|lambda_i\| <= (1-delta)(R_e + 7/2) for a fixed delta > 0, i.e. E_(i+1)/E_i = c_i(x) t^-(R_e+7/2) with slowly varying c_i. | Conjecture: at e = 2 (prediction -9.5) Re kappa in [-9.52, -6.84] at 11 of 12 balanced roots (one at -3.29); at e = 4 (prediction -31.5) Re kappa in [-32.0, -21.4] at 37 of 38, one exception at -417-264i (research/results/bmd-20261004-q/). | [Last-step sector ratio](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-ratio) |
| `lem:cube-far-sector-polynomial` | In the x-side sector decomposition at non-real r with its cuts, the sector polynomial E(z; r) = det[c] with each of the 4l mixed rows replaced by I_-1 + z I_0 equals sum_s E_s(r) z^s (degree at most 4l) and E(1; r) = det[c(r)], which has the roots of W_k off the branch points; if r_0 is a root of W_k at which z = 1 is a simple root of E(.; r_0), the analytic root z_j(r) with z_j(r_0) = 1 satisfies d/dr E(1; r_0) = -d/dz E(1; r_0) z_j'(r_0), so r_0 is simple iff z_j'(r_0) != 0 (a reformulation). | Working proof: multilinearity in the mixed rows and the implicit function theorem. | [Sector polynomial](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-polynomial) |
| `conj:cube-far-sector-extreme-laplace` | Hypothesis (refuted at e = 2, 4): each x-side sector sum E_s at the last step is dominated by the Laplace term in which the 0-sector rows take the top (or the bottom) block of columns. | Refutation: at 33 balanced roots (e = 2, 4) neither extreme term approximates E_s in any of 132 comparisons; 112 negligible, 20 comparable or larger by up to 1e130 (research/results/bmd-20261004-r/x-laplace.txt). | [Sector polynomial](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-polynomial) |
| `lem:cube-far-sector-multiple-integral` | With the x-side sector decomposition at non-real r (k' rows f_i, n = R_e), E(z; r) = (2 pi i)^(-k') times the k'-fold integral over Gamma_1 x ... x Gamma_k' of prod_i f_i(y_i)(y_i - r)^(-n-1) prod_(i<i') (1/(y_i' - r) - 1/(y_i - r)), where Gamma_i is a small circle about r for a pure row and K_-1 + z K_0 for a mixed row. | Working proof: entries as contour integrals, multilinearity in rows, and the Vandermonde det[w_i^s] with w = 1/(y - r). | [Sector gas](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-gas) |
| `conj:cube-far-sector-circle-count` | For every e >= 2, with the cuts of lem:cube-far-x-sector-decomposition and balance threshold 1e-3, each of the four consecutive sector pairs (E_i, E_(i+1)) balances at exactly R_e non-real roots of the last-step far polynomial W_(b-1); the other deg W_(b-1) - 4 R_e roots are real or unbalanced. | Conjecture: exactly 6 = R_2 per pair at e = 2 and 28 = R_4 per pair at e = 4, every non-real root passing the independent split control after a geometric hairpin guard (research/results/bmd-20261004-t/). | [Sector gas](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-gas) |
| `conj:cube-far-cluster-ratio` | At the last even-peeling step, at all but O(1) roots where consecutive x-side sector sums E_s, E_(s+1) balance, kappa_s = r(1+r) d/dr log(E_(s+1)/E_s) = -n - 15/2 + 2s + r(4s - 6) + o(1) as e -> infinity (n = R_e); equivalently E_(s+1)/E_s = C_s t^(-n-15/2+2s) (1+x)^(4s-6) (1+o(1)) locally with C_s constant, as predicted by moving one charge between the endpoint clusters of the sector log-gas. | Conjecture from a cluster heuristic: median \|kappa - prediction\| 0.79 at e = 2 (12 balanced roots) and 0.46 at e = 4 (38), against 1.34 and 1.49 for the flat value -(n+7/2); the largest error grows from 4.0 to 5.5, and one exceptional root (research/results/bmd-20261004-u/). | [Cluster ratio law](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-cluster-ratio) |
| `lem:cube-far-concave-balance` | If nonzero complex E_0..E_K (K >= 2) sum to zero and L_s = log\|E_s\| has all second differences <= -delta with delta >= log(2K^2), then with m the maximizer and m' its larger neighbour, \|E_m'\| >= \|E_m\|/2 and \|E_s\| <= 2 e^(-delta) \|E_m\| for every other s. | Working proof: monotonicity of concave sequences away from the maximum, x >= 1/K from the vanishing sum, concavity bounds at m and m', and x >= 1 - K^2 e^(-delta). | [Sector concavity](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-concavity) |
| `conj:cube-far-sector-concavity` | At the last even-peeling step, at all but O(e) roots of W_(b-1), the x-side sector sums satisfy log\|E_(s+1)\| - 2 log\|E_s\| + log\|E_(s-1)\| = -4 log(n+1) + 2 log\|r(1+r)\| + O(1) uniformly for 0 < s < 4 (n = R_e). | Conjecture, the r-part from the cluster exponents and the n-part an empirical fit: at e = 4 all 48 sampled roots strictly concave, second differences -16.0..-0.42, deviation median 0.96 (quartiles 0.67, 1.23), gap >= log 32 at 38 of 48; at e = 2, 12 of 13 concave (research/results/bmd-20261004-v/concavity.txt). | [Sector concavity](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-sector-concavity) |
| `conj:cube-far-certificate-scaling` | At the last even-peeling step, at all but O(e) balanced roots of W_(b-1), the x-side sector sums satisfy eps = \|R/E_i\| = O(n^-4 \|r(1+r)\|^2), eps' = \|R'\|\|r(1+r)\|/(N\|E_i\|) = O(e eps) and C = \|E_(i+1)'/E_(i+1)\|\|r(1+r)\|/N = O(e) (n = R_e, N = n + 7/2), so that, with \|kappa_i\| >= delta N (conj:cube-far-x-sector-ratio), eps' + eps C < \|kappa\|/N and the balance certificate of lem:cube-far-balance-certificate holds there for every large e. | Conjecture: the certificate inequality holds numerically (not rigorously) at all 24 (e = 2) and 56 conjugate-pair (e = 4) sampled balanced roots, log10 margin >= 1.03 and 1.06; median eps 8.8e-5 and 6.8e-7, C median 21.4 and 28.5 (research/results/bmd-20261004-w/). | [Balance certificate at the last step](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-04-cube-last-far-certificate) |

Then its minimal generators other than F have degree sum ((n-1)(2 lambda + 1) - lambda)/2 for n minimal generators; for n = 4 this is (5 lambda + 3)/2 (39 at d = 2, 139 at d = 3). | Conjecture: holds at d = 2 (generators 12,13,14,15, relations 17,18,19 for both T_2 and its link). | `lem:cube-far-degree-growth-obstruction` | For every n >= 1 and nonzero polynomials h_k(w), the family h_k R_(n,k) satisfies no linear recurrence in k with coefficients in Q[k,w] (leading coefficient nonzero), because such recurrences allow only linear growth of deg_w while deg R_(n,k) = (k-1)((3n-2)k+n^2-7n+4)/2 is quadratic; likewise for recurrences in n at fixed k >= 2. | Working proof from thm:cube-merge-far-count's degree formula; closes the classical Beraha-Kahane-Weiss route to simplicity of the far polynomials; q-type recurrences with coefficients in Q[w, w^k] are not excluded. | [Far degree-growth obstruction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-far-degree-growth) |
| `check:cube-contact-structured-planes` | Over F_211, separated points: on the polynomial-node plane (a_i = s + t i + u i^2 + v i^3) the contact locus K is empty at N = 7 and at N = 8, 9 consists of the reflection-symmetric line z = -y/(3m) plus two further set-symmetric points; on the geometric-node plane (2^i, 4^i, 8^i) at N = 9 it is empty. | Finite check (research/results/bmd-20261006-h/): every K point found lies in the symmetric locus, as conj:cube-offcollision-contact-bound predicts via lem:cube-symmetry-restatement; separated F_p-points only, closure not tested. | [Contact structured planes](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-contact-structured-planes) |
| `lem:cube-geometric-cone-collapse` | For N >= 3, delta > 0, \|q\| < delta/9 and (t,u,v) != 0 with \|f(q^i)\| >= delta max(\|t\|\|q\|^i, \|u\|\|q\|^(2i), \|v\|\|q\|^(3i)) for i <= N-1 (f(x) = t x + u x^2 + v x^3), the configuration a_i = s + f(q^i) is separated and its nested coordinates at the caterpillar point of M_(0,N+1) (mark at infinity) satisfy \|x_i\| <= 9\|q\|/delta; so such points converge to the caterpillar point uniformly as q -> 0. | Working proof (reviewed, after a failed first draft) by a geometric decay estimate in nested coordinates; it reduces, conditionally on three listed gaps, the cone form of lem:cube-contact-plane-criterion for the geometric cone at small q to avoidance by the closure of K of the caterpillar point and of the strata reached along the cancellation curves, which are not yet identified. | [Geometric cone collapse](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-geometric-cone-collapse) |
| `cor:cube-caterpillar-contact-avoidance` | Characteristic zero, every N >= 2 and every ordering: each caterpillar point of M_(0,N+1) (mark at infinity) has a neighbourhood on which every separated configuration has rank A_(R-1) = R; hence it lies outside the closure of the contact locus K and of the codimension-one locus rank A_(R-1) < R. | Working proof from thm:cube-caterpillar-minimality by curve selection and translation/dilation invariance; the multivariate form det A_(R-1) = x^e u(x), u(0) != 0, is an unproved sketch of the same mechanism (rediscovery), checked exactly at N = 4, 5. | `check:cube-tie-fcurve-low-contact` | For a_j = eps^j (2<=j<=N-1), a_N = 0, a_1 = c eps^i, the lowest eps-coefficient L_i(c) of det A_(R-1) has, besides c = 0, 1: N=4: c=-1 (i=2), none (i=3); N=5: c=-1 and 7c^2+2c+7 (i=2), c=-1 (i=3), none (i=4); N=6, i=2: the palindromic sextic 429c^6+594c^5+675c^4+700c^3+675c^2+594c+429. | Finite check over Q[c,eps] (research/results/bmd-20261006-k/); the low-contact divisor meets tie F-curves at finitely many points, so the caterpillar argument does not extend to them. | [Tie F-curves](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-fcurves) |

| `conj:cube-tie-window-full-rank` | For every m >= 1 and c != 0, 1, the (2m+1) x (2m+3) matrix of the coefficients of T^k, binom(m,2) <= k <= binom(m,2)+2m+2, of T^n (1+cT)^(-3/2), T^n (1+T)^(-3/2) (0 <= n < m) and ((1+cT)(1+T))^(-3/2) has full rank; via the top-tie block reduction this would keep the contact locus K away from tie F-curve points. | Conjecture: verified exactly over Q[c] for m <= 8 (gcd of maximal minors 1 off c = 0, 1); the square window reproduces the directly computed tie coefficients at N = 4, 5, 6; a norm argument fails; the reduction itself is a mechanism, not yet a proof. | [Tie window](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window) |

If f = Delta_(2m) + Delta_(2m+1) is not identically zero and f / (c^a (c-1)^b), with these factors fully removed, has all zeros in the open unit disc, then W'(c) and the tie contact window have full rank 2m+1 for every complex c != 0, 1 (characteristic zero). | Working proof: the substitution T = cS gives Delta_J(1/c) = +- c^e Delta_J(c) for every column set J, so common zeros of Delta_(2m), Delta_(2m+1) are closed under inversion and cannot all lie inside the disc. | [Tie window stability](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-schur-stability) |

| `lem:cube-tie-window-kernel-orthogonality` | For m >= 2 and complex c != 0, the Cramer kernel polynomial V_c(x) = sum_j (-1)^j Delta_j x^j of the tie window W'(c) satisfies contour orthogonality against x^(R''+1/2-n)(x+c)^(-3/2), x^(R''+1/2-n)(x+1)^(-3/2) (n < m) and x^(R''+2)(x+c)^(-3/2)(x+1)^(-3/2) around the cuts [-c,0], [-1,0]; sigma(c) = Delta_(2m)/Delta_(2m+1) is its zero sum, f_m = Delta_(2m+1)(1+sigma), sigma(1/c) = sigma(c)/c, and c^(-1/2) sigma(c) is real on \|c\| = 1. | Working proof: Cramer's rule, coefficient extraction as a contour integral with x = 1/T, Vieta, and the inversion symmetry of lem:cube-tie-window-stability-criterion with exponents differing by one. | [Tie window kernel](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-kernel-orthogonality) |
| `conj:cube-tie-window-wronskian` | For every m >= 2, with L_m, D_m the stripped last two tie-window minors, Q_m = 2c(D_m' L_m - D_m L_m') - D_m L_m equals (c-1) R_m with R_m having no zero on \|c\| = 1; equivalently (D_m, L_m being palindromic, checked exactly for m <= 6) the theta-Wronskian of the real functions e^(-i(d+1)theta/2) D_m, e^(-i d theta/2) L_m vanishes on (0, 2 pi) nowhere, so their zeros there strictly interlace. | Conjecture: verified exactly for m = 2..6 (Cayley-transform gcd certificate: no zero of R_m on \|c\| = 1; R_m irreducible of degree 2 binom(m,2), numerically half its zeros inside the circle; research/results/bmd-20261006-t/). | [Tie window kernel](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-kernel-orthogonality) |
| `lem:cube-tie-window-circle-crossing` | For every m >= 2 and non-integer lambda > 0 (exponent lambda in place of 3/2 in the tie window): every zero of f = Delta_(2m) + Delta_(2m+1) on \|c\| = 1 other than c = 1 is a common zero of these two minors; on an interval of non-integer lambda with constant stripped powers a, b of c, c-1, constant degree of f~ = f/(c^a(c-1)^b), and no common zero of the two minors on the circle minus {1}, the number of zeros of the stripped f in the unit disc is constant, so stability at one exponent propagates. | Working proof: reality of c^(-1/2) sigma on the circle for every real lambda (inversion symmetry and kernel lemma), then Hurwitz continuity of zeros. | [Tie window crossing](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-circle-crossing) |

| `lem:cube-tie-window-four-term-stability` | For every m >= 2, with d = binom(m,2), S = m^3+m^2-1, A = m^2+m+1, B = 2m+1, the polynomial g_m = ((S+A)/2) c^(d+1) + ((S-A)/2) c^d + ((S+B)/2) c + (S-B)/2 has all d+1 zeros in the open unit disc. | Working proof: on \|c\| = 1, \|c^d(alpha c+beta)\|^2 - \|gamma c+delta\|^2 = ((A^2-B^2)/2)(1-cos theta) >= 0 with g_m(1) = 2S != 0, so the symmetric Rouche theorem compares g_m with c^d(alpha c+beta). | [Tie window log limit](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-log-limit) |
| `conj:cube-tie-window-log-limit-closed-form` | For every m >= 3 the lambda -> 0 limit of the tie-window stability polynomial, Delta_(2m) + Delta_(2m+1) of the matrix of T^n log(1+cT), T^n log(1+T) (n < m) and log(1+cT) log(1+T) on columns binom(m,2)..binom(m,2)+2m+1, equals a nonzero constant times c^a (c-1)^b g_m, with g_m the four-term polynomial of lem:cube-tie-window-four-term-stability. | Conjecture: exact for m = 3..7 (research/results/bmd-20261006-v/); the cubic coefficients were fitted to these five values, so each fit is tested by one extra value. | [Tie window log limit](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-log-limit) |
| `conj:cube-tie-window-log-minor-closed-forms` | For every m >= 3, d = binom(m,2), E = binom(m+2,2), alpha = m(m+1)^2/2, gamma = m(m^2+m+2)/2: the lambda -> 0 log tie-window minors satisfy Delta_(2m+1) = kappa c^a (c-1)^b E (c^d + 1) and Delta_(2m) = -kappa c^a (c-1)^b (alpha (c^(d+1)+1) + gamma (c^d + c)); hence their sum is -kappa c^a (c-1)^b g_m, the limit tie zeros are the d-th roots of -1, and the limit pair interlaces on the unit circle. | Conjecture: exact for m = 3..7 (research/results/bmd-20261006-x/), with the m = 8 sum confirmed; it implies conj:cube-tie-window-log-limit-closed-form, and the interlacing consequence follows by a short trigonometric computation recorded in the entry. | [Tie window log minors](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-window-log-minors) |
| `lem:cube-tie-log-square-orders` | For m >= 1, s >= m, the square log matrix M_(m,s)(x,y) (rows x^(k-n)/(k-n), y^(k-n)/(k-n), n < m, and sum_i x^i y^(k-i)/(i(k-i)), columns s..s+2m) has determinant a binary form of degree (2m+1)s + m^2 + 2m, of exact order m(s+1) in x and in y and of order at least m(m+1)/2 along x = y; hence it equals K x^(m(s+1)) y^(m(s+1)) (x-y)^(m^2) (x^s + y^s), K != 0, once the diagonal order m^2 and the divisibility by x^s + y^s are known. | Working proof: homogeneity; Laplace expansion with Cauchy determinants after reducing the top row to sum_(i>=m) (x^i/i) B_i; Taylor expansion along x = y with a Hall-type count of rational components; degree count. | [Log square binomial](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-06-cube-tie-log-square-binomial) |

| `thm:cube-tie-log-window-closed-forms` | For m >= 1 and s >= m, on the log window (rows T^n log(1+xT), T^n log(1+yT), n < m, and log(1+xT)log(1+yT); columns s..s+2m+1): det N = K x^(ms) y^(ms) (x-y)^(m^2) for the single-log block N; the square minor is (-1)^(s+m)(m-1)! B(s,m+1) (s+m)!/(s+2m)! x^m y^m (x^s+y^s) det N; and the second minor over the square minor is -(s(x^(s+1)+y^(s+1)) + m(s+m+1)(x+y)(x^s+y^s))/((s+2m+1)(x^s+y^s)). | `conj:cube-deep-row-reduction` | For a tie over r deep roots (M = r + 2, valuations nu_1 < ... < nu_r) and a cross coordinate set with p <= r negative indices (window negatives, or an invertible leading block): after divided differences A_i = V[beta_1..beta_i], C_i = (U - 1)A_i (extracting the deep Vand^2), the leading vectors of C_1..C_p on the negative columns are independent, and a triangular reduction with nonnegative-valuation coefficients polynomial in eps leaves each C_i (i > p) with residual eps-coefficients of valuation at least 2 sum_(a <= i-p) nu_a. | Conjecture: for r = 2, p = 1 it is lem:cube-small-pair-order; at M = 5 (r = 3, nu = (1,2,3)) the penalty thresholds 28, 16, 10 implied for p = 0, 1, 2 hold on all 286 coordinate sets of ten columns in [-2, 10], attained at the windows (q-adic check at one point, conclusive for refutation only; residuals not measured). | [Deep row reduction](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-08-cube-deep-row-reduction) |

| `thm:cube-cherry-hankel-form` | For every M >= 2 and 1 <= j <= M, the coefficient of u^(B_j), B_j = j^2 - j + M, in the cherry cross coordinate on the window [-j, 2M-1-j] (x = 1, eps = u, lambda = 3/2) is Vand(y)^2 c_(M,j) Hank_(M-j)(y), with \|c_(M,j)\| = \|H_j c_1^k prod_(e<j) c_e prod_(i<2M-j) c_i\| 2^(-k) (M-k-1)!/(M+k)!, k = M - j, H_j the binomial Hankel determinant; c_(M,j) != 0. | Working proof: the u-minimal terms form one determinant; the negative columns factor through det[c_(e+k)] = H_j; column operations with P = prod(z - y_s) reduce to the neck-block matrix K = [[z^m] rem(int_0 z^n P, P)], whose determinant is (M-k-1)!/(M+k)! | `lem:cube-cross-hypergeometric-alternant` | Every cherry cross coordinate (x = 1, eps = u) equals, as a power series in u, a constant times Vand(y) times det[u^n F_n(u y_s) (n in N) \| sum_i (P v_j)_i y_s^i F_i(u y_s)/c_i (j < k)]_s, F_n(w) = sum_m c_m c_(n+m) w^m = c_n 2F1(3/2, n+3/2; n+1; w), with P v_j a basis of the multiples of P in C(Pol_Lambda+); for windows v_j = z^j and the constant is a nonzero rational. | Working proof: the kernel decomposition of thm:cube-graded-hankel-penalty, with each column's remainder replaced by its values at the roots; numerical check of the window case for M <= 4 to u^(B+6) at two points; exact window coefficients at M = 3 for t <= 3. | [Hypergeometric alternant](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-window-hypergeometric-alternant) |

| `prop:cube-window-local-exchange-reduction` | Along an arc, let omega(Lambda) be the valuation of the cherry cross Plücker coordinate P_Lambda. If some window is a minimizer, and every minimizer inside an interval I of 2M+1 columns has no single exchange of smaller value and only tying exchanges inside I, then every minimizer lies in I, so (W') holds on the arc. | `lem:cube-three-leader-slack` | Under the hypotheses of prop:cube-cherry-step-wide with the leading cross vector supported on three sets A_c + {b_j}, \|A_c\| = 2M-1, leading coefficients kappa_j: the limit space is the coordinate space on R-1 exponents plus one vector v with coordinates eps_j kappa_j on the exponents beta_j = -lambda + b_j, and the slack is 0 iff (eps_j kappa_j) is proportional to the Lagrange weights gamma_j = 1/prod_(a in A, a != beta_j)(beta_j - a). | Working proof: the annihilator of the leading cross space lies in the span of the three dual coordinates, so the space is a coordinate block plus a line; the order-(R+1) element of the enlarged space has the Lagrange weights as coordinates. | [Wide cherry step](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-cherry-step-wide) |

| `lem:cube-topup-translation-equation` | In the cherry setting, for 1 <= p <= M-1, the least coefficients W_p of the window Lambda_p and tau°_p of the top-up T_p, as polynomials in the reparametrized roots y', satisfy d_tr tau°_p = -(lambda + 2M - p - 1) W_p (d_tr = sum d/dy'_i); hence conj:cube-topup-flow-identity is equivalent to the vanishing of the translation-invariant remainder tau_p - kappa_(M,p) (D + 2k e1) Hank_k with kappa_(M,p) = -(lambda + 2M - p - 1) c_(M,p) / (2k(M + k + 1)), k = M - p. | Working proof: equivariance of the cross Pluecker vector under dilations about the cherry root (generator e_t -> (lambda+t)(e_(t+1) - e_t), lowering on coordinates), parameter generator -(1/x) d_tr - E on polynomials in y', comparison at x^(A_p) eps^(B_p); consistent with the exact data at M = 3, 4. | [Top-up translation equation](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-topup-translation-equation) |

| `thm:cube-schur-hankel-termination` | For M >= 2, 1 <= k <= M-1, y in C^M, H_(b) = sum_(\|S\|=k+1) Vand(y_S)^2 h_b(y_S): sum_b H_(b) z^b = A(z)/prod_i (1 - y_i z) with A = sum_S Vand(y_S)^2 prod_(i not in S)(1 - y_i z) of degree <= M-k-1, so all H_(b) vanish iff H_(0..M-k-1) do (the set Omega_k); Omega_k is invariant under y -> alpha y + c; real clusters with k+1 distinct entries have Hank_k > 0; affine images of the M-th roots of unity lie in Omega_k for 2 <= k <= M-2. With thm:cube-single-shift-schur-hankel, off Omega_k some window raised by t <= p-1 has a nonzero least coefficient (whether it leads over other shapes is open). | Working proof (generating function, affine transformation of G, weighted Cauchy-Binet and a rank bound J + E at roots of unity); exact checks: the identity at random clusters for M <= 6 (parts 2, 3 untested), and Omega_k at roots of unity exactly for 2 <= k <= M-2, M <= 9 (research/results/bmd-20261009-keu/termination.txt); reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Schur-Hankel termination](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-schur-hankel-termination) |
| `lem:cube-polygon-raise-selection` | In the cherry setting, for L = {-p..-1} u J with J a set of N = 2M-p nonnegative columns and E+ = sum J - C(N,2), the coefficient of x^(A_p+E+) eps^(B_p) in P_L is Vand^2 tau_L with tau_L symmetric and homogeneous of degree k(k+1)+E+; hence at the M-th roots of unity (centred at 0) tau_L = 0 unless M divides k(k+1)+E+. | Working proof (homogeneity in x y_s, symmetry under exchange of roots, the window's degree); reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Polygon raise selection](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-polygon-raise-selection) |

| `thm:cube-polygon-schur-hankel-residue` | For M >= 2, 1 <= k <= M-1 and every partition mu with at most k+1 parts, at the M-th roots of unity H_mu = sum_(\|S\|=k+1) Vand(y_S)^2 s_mu(y_S) equals +-M^(k+1) if the exponents mu + delta have residues exactly {0, -1, ..., -k} mod M, and 0 otherwise; the least weight of a nonzero H_mu is k(M-k-1), attained only by the rectangle ((M-k-1)^k). | Working proof (bialternant and Cauchy-Binet: H_mu = +- det[p_(a+b)], a permutation-or-singular 0/1 matrix at roots of unity); exact check of 298 cases, M = 4, 5, \|mu\| <= 8 (research/results/bmd-20261009-kex/residue-criterion.txt); reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Polygon residue criterion](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-polygon-residue-theorem) |
| `thm:cube-polygon-rectangle-raise` | For M >= 2, 1 <= k <= M-1, p = M-k, at the regular M-gon centred at 0: raising the top k columns of the cherry window Lambda_p by a partition lambda with at most k parts and lambda_1 <= p gives a nonzero least coefficient if and only if lambda = ((p-1)^k), of weight k(M-k-1). | Working proof (eliminators z^i - (z^i mod P) = g_i P, complete homogeneous h_j = [M \| j] at the polygon, Jacobi minor of Pi with only diagonal and p_M entries: permutation for C = {p..M-1}, two rows on one column otherwise); numerical checks at the pentagon and heptagon, including lambda_1 > p (research/results/bmd-20261009-key/raised-tops.txt); reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Rectangle raise](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-polygon-rectangle-raise) |

| `thm:cube-raise-triangularity` | For M >= 1, 1 <= p <= M, k = M - p and every partition lambda with at most k parts, let I(lambda) = [0, M-1] u {M + n + lambda_(k-n) : n < k} (the window's nonnegative part with its top k columns raised by lambda). The minor Delta_(I(lambda)) of the coefficient matrix of V_p(y) (prop:cube-family-schubert-reduction; the least coefficient of the cherry set [-p,-1] u I(lambda) up to a nonzero constant and Vand^2) equals c_lambda pi_lambda + sum over mu strictly inside lambda of f_(lambda mu)(y) pi_mu, with c_lambda a nonzero constant, f polynomials, and pi_mu the maximal minors of the moment matrix (p_(r+c))_(r >= 0, c <= k). | Working proof: eliminators z^T - rem(z^T, P) = sum h_(T-M-m) z^m P, Cauchy-Binet over the F_m with a unitriangular h-matrix at J_lambda, the tau-reduction and Jacobi minors of Pi, generalized Laplace expansion along the staircase rows; prediction test at a non-rotation block quintic (every raise not containing the block rectangle vanishes); reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Ramification equals flow order](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-ramification-flow-order-proof) |

| `thm:cube-cblock-failure-hypersurface` | Characteristic zero, every M, every distinct-root point y* with j = j_F(y*) >= 1 (flow order of the Taylor cofactor F), analytic arcs y~'(s) = y* + s v + O(s^2) and Puiseux x = x1 s^w + ..., x1 != 0: the first-order data (v, x1) on which the C-block's leading space E has positive weight at the mark are none for w < 1/j, exactly the hypersurface dF(y*) v + gamma x1^j = 0 for w = 1/j (gamma = [t^j] F(y*/(1 + t y*)) != 0), and contained in the tangent hyperplane dF(y*) v = 0 for w > 1/j (a proper condition when dF(y*) != 0); at w = 1/j on transverse arcs the leading C-support is exactly {T_0, S_0}. | Working proof: least valuation of the C-block coordinates from wt_0(V(y*)) = j_F and Gale minimality (prop:cube-cblock-spread-bound), the flowed-arc criterion (prop:cube-cblock-flowed-arc), and the Newton polygon of F along the flowed arc (single edge from (1,0) to (0,j)); at j = 1 it is cor:cube-cblock-tie-hyperplane; reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [C-block failure hypersurface](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-cblock-weight-hypersurface) |
| `thm:cube-two-set-tie-avoidance` | Characteristic zero, every M, cherry-step setting: if the leading C-block support is two sets (necessarily a single exchange S, S - sigma + tau, by basis exchange; any tau > sigma) and the cross block has a unique leader, the limit pair space L0 has weight at most 1 at the mark, its orders lie in [0, R] (either [0, R-1] or [0, R-2] u {R}), and the arc avoids K. | Working proof: by lem:cube-leading-wronskian-sum the Taylor minors on [0, R-1] and [0, R-2] u {R} are sum_X pi_X Vand(X u Z) and sum_X pi_X Vand(X u Z)(Sum(X u Z) - binom(R,2)) up to constants (falling factorials and Jacobi-Trudi); when the first vanishes the second is -alpha_S (tau - sigma) != 0; no transversality hypothesis; matches the recorded control orders 0..13, 15; reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Two-set tie avoidance](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-two-set-tie-avoidance) |

| `thm:cube-excess-failure-codimension` | Characteristic zero, every M, cherry-step setting: if the leading C-support and cross support have unions exceeding a basis by e_C and e_U columns (e = e_C + e_U), the arc avoids K if e <= 2, and, when e_C <= 2M+2 and e_U <= R_C+2, it avoids K unless the leading spaces (E, U) lie in a closed subvariety of Gr(R_C, E~) x Gr(2M, U~) of codimension at least 3 (E~, U~ the coordinate spaces on the unions). | Working proof: containment of L0 in the coordinate space X on the unions (dimension R + e, consecutive orders), avoidance unless L0 meets the (e-2)-dimensional subspace W of elements of order >= R+2, and an incidence count over P(W) with Schubert conditions of codimension e_C and e_U; reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Excess failure codimension](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-excess-failure-codimension) |

| `lem:cube-frobenius-planted-excess` | For every multi-index n = (n_0; n_1..n_6) with n_6 >= 1 and any power series f_1..f_5, the series f_6 = T^(\|n\|+2) - p_0 - sum_(g<=5) p_g f_g (any p_g with deg p_g < n_g) makes 1, f_1..f_6 admit the form T^(\|n\|+2), so the Hermite-Pade determinants H(n'') vanish on the whole excess-two simplex n <= n'', \|n''\| <= \|n\|+2, while the three-term identity of lem:cube-window-hermite-pade-frobenius (2) holds; with f_1..f_5 the actual triple-window functions at m = 2 the planted system keeps all 431 determinants on the faces below n nonzero, as the true system does, so identity, block pattern and boundary values cannot exclude excess-two blocks. | Working proof: explicit planting and the left-kernel argument of lem:cube-window-hermite-pade-frobenius (1); exact boundary check at m = 2 (results/bmd-20261009-kfn/planted-boundary.txt); reviewed by one fresh-context medium reviewer. | [Padé block lead closed](https://kbr.is-a.dev/math-research/branches/binary-multiplicity-degree/#entry-2026-10-09-cube-pade-block-lead-closed) |
